title: [bug] SSR: CJS module instantiated twice when resolved via different specifier formats by a plugin
body:
### Describe the bug

During Server-Side Rendering (SSR), Vite's module runner instantiates a CommonJS module twice if it is imported using two different specifier formats that are resolved to the same file by a custom resolveId plugin.
In our use case with Deno, a plugin resolves both a bare specifier (noop-tag) and a prefixed specifier (npm:noop-tag) to the exact same CJS file on disk. However, Vite's SSR module graph does not seem to recognize them as the same module, leading to two separate initializations.
This breaks any CJS package that relies on a singleton pattern or shared module-level state, most notably React, where it leads to the infamous "Invalid hook call" error because the useState hook is called from a different module instance than the one that initiated the render.


### Reproduction

https://github.com/nestarz/deno-vite-issue-2/tree/main

### Steps to reproduce

I have created a minimal reproducible example that uses a simple CJS package instead of React to isolate the issue. The package generates a random id upon initialization. The server entry point imports this package using both specifier styles and compares the IDs. The fact that the IDs are different proves the module was instantiated twice.

deno task dev --force 
Go to http://localhost:8000/

#### Root Cause Analysis

After further investigation, the root cause appears to be the interaction between Vite's default SSR externalization behavior and our custom resolution plugin.

Here is the sequence of events that leads to the double instantiation:

1.  **Bare Specifier (`noop-tag`):** When Vite's SSR loader encounters `import state from "noop-tag"`, it identifies `"noop-tag"` as a bare module specifier. By default, Vite externalizes bare specifiers for SSR. The module is loaded directly by the underlying Node.js runtime's `require()` mechanism and its instance is managed by Node's module cache.

2.  **Plugin-Resolved Specifier (`npm:noop-tag`):** When the loader encounters `import state from "npm:noop-tag"`, our custom `deno()` plugin's `resolveId` hook intercepts it. The plugin resolves this specifier to an **absolute file path** on disk (e.g., `/path/to/project/node_modules/.deno/noop-tag@2.0.1/.../index.js`).

3.  **Divergent Loading Paths:** Because the result of the second resolution is an absolute file path and not a bare specifier, **Vite does not externalize it**. Instead, Vite processes and evaluates this module using its own internal SSR module runner (`vite:ssr-load-module`).

This results in the same CJS module file being loaded by two different systems: **Node's native loader** (for the externalized bare specifier) and **Vite's SSR runner** (for the plugin-resolved path). Each system maintains its own separate module cache, leading to two distinct module instances and causing the observed bug.

title: Wrong esbuild target when using `vite dev`

### Describe the bug

When setting a build target in the config using either `build.target` or `esbuild.target`, this only applies to `vite build`. So far, this is expected, since #10207 automatically sets the esbuild target to `esnext` when using `vite dev`. title: Double invocation of `transform` when saving a file

### Describe the bug Hey! I'm one of the maintainers of Tailwind CSS and we ran into an issue with our `@tailwindcss/vite` plugin where the `App.css` file is processed twice when saving a single `App.tsx` file. I reproduced this by creating a minimal Vite plugin that looks like this: ```tsx function repro(): Plugin[] { return [ { name: '@tailwindcss/vite:generate:serve', apply: 'serve', enforce: 'pre', async transform(src, id, options) { // Assume that `@import "tailwindcss";` exists in `App.css`. title: Disabling WebSocket and HMR
body:
### Description

Some users are actively seeking ways to disable HMR (#13994).

With HML enabled, and reactive components are partially rendered, it is unpredictable #18217 when page reload happens.
From my personal experience, the page reloads multiple times, even during simple navigation within the project.


### Suggested solution

Please provide an option for users to disable WebSocket and HMR.
```
    server: {
        socket: false,
        hmr: false,
    },
```
A single page reload after updating code in the editor is sufficient and might be optimal solution.
Fortunately, Vite is capable of updating CSS and JS files even without WebSocket enabled.

### Alternative

![Screenshot 2024-10-28 at 05 35 52](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdb732f3-614f-479f-870c-325c1a327fbb)


### Additional context

Normally I do not change the library's code. However, this changes made my developing experience much more predictable and less annoying with unexpected reloads.
```
function setupWebSocket(protocol, hostAndPath, onCloseWithoutOpen) {
  if (!socketEnabled) return;
```

Thanks.

title: bug(ssr): vite hmr server called twice when use two configurations in server side render
body:
### Describe the bug

In vite ssr, if I separate vite config logic to different files like `vite.client.config.ts` and `vite.server.config.ts`, and I get `viteDevServer` instance by calling `createServer` method use these configurations.

On the server side, I use `ssrLoadModule` in the viteDevServer instance, like

```js
const viteServer = await createServer(serverConfig)
await (viteServer as ViteDevServer).ssrLoadModule(viteServerEntry)

On the client side, I use a ViteDevServer instance with middleware mode, like

const viteServer: ViteDevServer = await createServer(clientConfig)

title: WebWorker URL is not properly resolved in dev pre-bundled dependency
body:
### Describe the bug

I'm trying to use the `@aztec/bb.js` library that has an asynchronous function that loads a web worker, using the regular syntax:
```js
const worker = new Worker(new URL('./main.worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' });
```

Unfortunately, it seems vite pre-bundling breaks when this function is actually called, as the URL ends up being rewritten as `node_modules/.vite/deps/main.worker.js?worker_file&type=module`, which doesn't actually exist (it does get rewritten, as you can see, so that's not the issue itself, but the path is incorrect).

I do get the helpful error below, which ends up working (see commented out code in repro-directory vite.config.ts).
```
The file does not exist at "node_modules/.vite/deps/main.worker.js?worker_file&type=module" which is in the optimize deps directory. The dependency might be incompatible with the dep optimizer. Try adding it to `optimizeDeps.exclude`.
```
If I exclude the dependency, things work out as the relative paths are preserved.

Opening the issue because this seems like a somewhat common problem potentially, and I'm not 100% sure where it goes wrong - maybe vite just confuses the path of the prebundled dependency with the path of the original query, in which case maybe the worker URL should be rewritten when pre-bundling? Maybe some other thing.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/hyli-org/vite-bb-worker-issue

title: CSS Modules 场景下 :global 里的 keyframes 失效
Support --force (and/or pass-through of Vite flags) in vike CLI
body:
### Description

## Context
Vike CLI currently supports only the options `--host`, `--port`, and `--mode`.  
Other Vite CLI flags such as `--force` aren’t available. This makes cache-busting flows awkward compared to using the Vite CLI directly.

Reference: [Vike CLI docs](https://vike.dev/cli) – only the three options above are listed as supported.

## Expected
Running:
```bash
vike dev --force
vike build --force
````

should behave like Vite (ignoring prebundled cache and forcing a fresh build).

## Actual

`vike` ignores `--force`; only the three aliased flags are recognized.

## Why it matters

* Developer ergonomics: quickly fixing stale prebundle/cache issues without custom scripts.
* Parity with Vite CLI expectations (`--force` is common in Vite workflows).
* Keeps one entry point (`vike`) instead of swapping back to `vite` just to use CLI flags.

## Workarounds

* Manually remove the cache folder:

  ```bash
  rm -rf node_modules/.vite && vike dev
  ```
* Configure `cacheDir` in `vite.config.ts` or add a pre-script that wipes `.vite`.



## Proposal

* Add `--force` as a supported Vike setting, similar to `--host`, `--port`, and `--mode`.
* (Optional) Provide a generic pass-through mechanism for other Vite flags, so users don’t hit this again for flags like `--clearScreen`.

title: Respect Browserslist config in esbuild
body:
### Description

esbuild doesn’t have built-in Browserslist config.

Benefits:
* Autoprefixer, postcss-preset-env, Babel and many other tools have. So users may expect Browserslist config.
* It is great to have only single config to specify target browsers for all tools.
* With Browserslist config, we can reduce polyfills in esbuild output and make JS works faster.

### Suggested solution

We can use [`browserslist-to-esbuild`](https://github.com/marcofugaro/browserslist-to-esbuild) as suggested in [When Vite ignores your Browserslist configuration](https://dev.to/meduzen/when-vite-ignores-your-browserslist-configuration-3hoe) article.

In this case, Vite will look for Browserslist config and auto-fill [`build.target`](https://vitejs.dev/config/build-options.html#build-target) config option.

### Alternative

_No response_

### Additional context

Browserslist also supports Node.js versions

body:

### Explain in Detail

I know I can exclude code from production by wrapping it in `if (import.meta.env.DEV) { /* exclude me */ }`. But it doesn't say this any where explicitly in the docs! 

I just spent 15 minutes looking for it in order to send links to my colleagues and ended up instead linking to this [comment in the issues](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/3110#discussioncomment-907109) and this [stack overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/a/76783737).

Surely this useful feature warrants a paragraph?

---
## Conditional Compilation

Code can be included only in certain modes by wrapping it in conditionals based on the Vite `import.meta.env` values. 

For example:
```
if (import.meta.env.DEV) {
 // code inside here will only be included when import.meta.env.DEV is true.
  console.log('Dev mode') 
}

title: The ability to predefine scaffolding parameters from the command line for `create-vite` and ask for the rest interactively
body:
### Description

I'm working on a template for applications. The template is built as a mono-repository, in which the UI is an independent package based on vite. 

In such a structure, the UI can be any option provided by `create-vite` tool, but there are still parts that needs to be properly setup.

For example, regardless of the UI stack, its package name must be specific so that other packages in the mono repository can refer to it. 

### Suggested solution

It would be useful to be able to predefine some parameters on the command line, such as the package name, and ask the user interactively during deployment.

```
npm create vite -- --set.packageName=@myrepo/name
```
This command will start interactive mode and ask user about framework and TS etc and skip prompt for package name.

### Alternative

title: Pseudo element selectors with nested @starting-style doesn't build correctly
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi,

When you have a nested `@starting-style` inside a pseudo-element selector, it works in development but doesn't work after the build, the CSS build output is wrong.

Here is an example:
```css
dialog {
  margin: auto;
}

dialog::backdrop {
  background: #2E368C7F;
  transition: opacity 1s ease-in;

  @starting-style {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

Here is the CSS output (after build):
```css
dialog{margin:auto}dialog::backdrop{background:#2e368c7f;transition:opacity 1s ease-in}@starting-style{{opacity:0}}
```
Formated output:
```css
dialog {
  margin: auto
}

dialog::backdrop {
  background: #2e368c7f;
  transition: opacity 1s ease-in
}

@starting-style {
    {
    opacity: 0
  }
}
```

The `@starting-style` get's placed outside the original selector. If the objective is to place it outside, it needs to have the pseudo-element selector inside it.

Placing the `@starting-style` inside a selector isn't invalid syntax: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@starting-style#syntax

It doesn't have to be `::backdrop`, it happens with any pseudo-element selector (e.g. `::after`, `::before`) based on my tests.

Reproduction:
[vite-nested-starting-style-bug-demo](https://github.com/machadinhos/vite-nested-starting-style-bug-demo)

Thank you!

我这里是使用递归的方法删除的 可以删除中文文件夹和文件

const removeFileSync = (filePath: string) => {

title: Expose more functions from `build`
body:
### Description

In our project, we use vite with some custom plugins. In one of these plugins, we need to bundle ourselves using rollup. Additionally, we need to pass the worker plugins to rollup. This works fine in vite 5. However, the changes to vite 6 (and also vite 7) introduces changes to how such plugins are applied in rollup. In particular, the following does not work anymore because the plugins are not properly applied:
```
// vite > 6
const bundle = await rollup.rollup({
   input: resolved.id, // pass in some custom `ResolvedId`
   plugins: plugins: config.worker.plugins // pass in the resolved config. In vite 5, we passed it with config.worker.plugins([]) which worked fine
```
We found in your source code in `worker.ts` that you apply the environment to the plugins using `injectEnvironmentToHooks`. Consequently, we made a custom build that exposes this function and got it to work.

Is there a specific reason that you don't expose this function? 
Is there a way to expose this function to the client?
And if not, is there a way to reproduce this behavior using the functions that vite exposes?

### Suggested solution

Please expose more functions to the client to work with the new `Environment API` or point us to how we can manually invoke rollup with vite plugins.

title: (Error) Vite in its latest version does not install the rollup module for android arm64
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi, I'm a small Front-end developer working from my Android phone since I don't have a PC or laptop. I've been doing my practice and projects from my phone, using React, Tailwind, HTML, and CSS for the time being. I use Termux as a terminal and to install and run my projects, etc. However, in this latest version of Vite, there's a problem running my React project (npm run dev). It says the Android Arm64 rollup module is needed, and Vite apparently didn't install it. This error didn't happen in previous versions, and I'd like to report this bug since some people don't have a PC to practice or run projects and have to use other alternatives.

In my case, I solved the error by pasting the code into Vite's package.json file to fix the rollup error.

This is the code I used to fix the installation error that Vite has on mobile devices, in my case, Android (which didn't happen in previous versions of Vite).

"overrides": {
"@rollup/rollup-android-arm64": "4.45.1"
}

Please, it would be a great help to fix this issue for future versions of Vite and better consider Android. Thanks for reading.

Please take more into account ARM, ARM64 and Android, because although it may not seem like it, people who use these alternatives do not necessarily do so for pleasure, but because not everyone can afford a laptop or PC to work or at least practice coding for personal reasons and have to require available alternatives. We appreciate that this issue be seen, taken into account and solved in future versions, thank you.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/4828

### Steps to reproduce

In my case, I solved the error by pasting the code into Vite's package.json file to fix the rollup error.

This is the code I used to fix the installation error that Vite has on mobile devices, in my case, Android (which didn't happen in previous versions of Vite).

"overrides": {
"@rollup/rollup-android-arm64": "4.45.1"
}

### System Info

```shell
The system where the error was found was Android when creating the React project with Vite, and Vite doesn't install the Android Arm64 rollup modules in the package.json.

In my case, as mentioned above, I use Termux.
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

_No response_

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1580c76-cb70-4eb3-b441-7f5af187521a)

This is the screenshot I took of the error before fixing it.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85aef7f2-fee3-461a-aabb-76e7873696ec)

And this is the screenshot from when I edited the package.json file and added the following code:

"overrides": {
"@rollup/rollup-android-arm64": "4.45.1"
}

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e22cbc7-153a-44af-9b1d-760653c6be1a)

title: Import files as direct bytearray
body:
### Description

I'm making a tool that allows reading NBT files, and NBT files are directly binary data. In order to provide a clear demonstration, I'm grabbing all files from my local `/resources` folder with a glob import, but whenever I use `?raw` or `{ as: "raw" }`, it corrupts the data when it turns it into a string.

This also seems to be a used use case for [other situations (stackoverflow)](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73847316/import-raw-image-data-into-a-script-with-vite) by other developers as well.

Do note that (if this enhancement is accepted), I am fully willing to implement this myself.

### Suggested solution

Provide a new query type, e.g. `?buffer` that loads the data as a `Uint8Array`.

### Alternative

I could make a new Vite plugin, but this seems useful enough to not mandate the use of a plugin.

title: Setting `css.preprocessorOptions.scss.fatalDeprecations` using a `Version` causes `obsolete` deprecations to log warnings
body:
### Describe the bug

My goal is to automatically set the `fatalDeprecations` using the current version of `sass` from our `package.json`. That way when it gets bumped, we are forced to fix those deprecations.

If I set `fatalDeprecations` using `Version.parse`, then all of the deprecations that are also obsolete are also getting added. This seems to cause the sass compiler to spit out warnings like the following

```
Warning: mixed-decls deprecation is obsolete, so does not need to be made fatal.

Warning: type-function deprecation is obsolete, so does not need to be made fatal
```

Adding `mixed-decls` and `type-functions` to `silenceDeprecations` causes the following warnings

```
Warning: mixed-decls deprecation is obsolete. If you were previously silencing it, your code may now behave in unexpected ways.

Warning: type-function deprecation is obsolete. If you were previously silencing it, your code may now behave in unexpected ways.
```

Ideally, `Version.parse` would not include any deprecations that are obsolete, so we can always use the latest version and be up-to-date on our deprecations.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-daxkrf7y?file=src%2Fmain.js

### Steps to reproduce

1) Add `sass` as a dependency
1) Set `css.preprocessorOptions.scss.fatalDeprecations` to `Version.parse("1.92.1")`
1) Make a `.scss` file and use it
1) Run either `vite build` or `vite` and see warnings

title: Terser nameCache is broken by multi-threaded mode, causing object key–value mismatches in different chunks
body: ### Describe the bug When nameCache is provided, it gets cloned for each worker thread, resulting in isolated caches that are not synchronized back to the main thread. This inconsistency can cause key–value mismatches for the same type of object in different chunks, making the `nameCache` ineffective and leading to incorrect minification results. ### Reproduction https://github.com/AntaresQAQ/vite-terser-bug-repro ### Steps to reproduce ### Vite Config ```ts import { defineConfig } from "vite"; const nameCache = {}; // https://vite.dev/config/ export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ { name: "terser-mangle-props-cache", closeBundle() { console.log("Name cache:", nameCache); }, }, ], build: { minify: "terser", terserOptions: { compress: false, mangle: { properties: true, }, nameCache, }, }, }); ``` ### Codes `obj1.ts` ```ts import type { IDemoObj } from "./types"; const obj: IDemoObj = { baz: "baz", foo: "foo", qux: "qux", bar: "bar", }; export default obj; ``` `src/obj2.ts` ```ts import type { IDemoObj } from "./types"; const obj: IDemoObj = { foo: "foo", bar: "bar", baz: "baz", qux: "qux", }; export default obj; ``` ### Built files 1. chunk `obj1-Ds7_RE47.js` ```js const a={o:"baz",t:"foo",u:"qux",q:"bar"};export{a as default}; ``` 2. chunk `obj2-DqD_p4d0.js` ```js const a={o:"foo",t:"bar",u:"baz",q:"qux"};export{a as default}; ``` ### Vite outputs ``` yarn run v1.22.22 $ tsc -b && vite build vite v7.1.5 building for production... ✓ 6 modules transformed. dist/index.html 0.39 kB │ gzip: 0.27 kB dist/assets/obj1-Ds7_RE47.js 0.06 kB │ gzip: 0.08 kB dist/assets/obj2-DqD_p4d0.js 0.06 kB │ gzip: 0.08 kB dist/assets/index-BJnHZlGe.js 2.21 kB │ gzip: 1.03 kB ✓ built in 171ms Name cache: {} ✨ Done in 0.84s. ``` ### Expected Result - the `obj1` is the same as `obj2`. - the `nameCache` is not empty. ### System Info ```shell System: OS: macOS 15.6.1 CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M2 Pro Memory: 263.14 MB / 32.00 GB Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 22.16.0 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.16.0/bin/node Yarn: 1.22.22 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.16.0/bin/yarn npm: 10.9.2 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.16.0/bin/npm Browsers: Chrome: 140.0.7339.133 Safari: 18.6 npmPackages: vite: ^7.1.2 => 7.1.5 ``` ### Used Package Manager yarn ### Logs _No response_ ### Validations - [x] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Read the [docs](https://vite.dev/guide). - [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. - [x] Make sure this is a Vite issue and not a framework-specific issue. title: "require is not defined" on the server, in dev mode only
body:
### Describe the bug

https://github.com/jakearchibald/vite-srr-require-bug-demo/commit/332d0aeb4fba39feb4071aebbff5f43bae1c0890 - here's a reduced example of the issue, building on top of the Preact SSR template.

Here I'm using a plugin to import a module for SSR only. In this case, JSDOM. `pnpm run build && pnpm run preview` works fine. However, if I visit the app in `pnpm run dev`, I get the error `ReferenceError: require is not defined`.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/jakearchibald/vite-srr-require-bug-demo/commit/332d0aeb4fba39feb4071aebbff5f43bae1c0890

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out https://github.com/jakearchibald/vite-srr-require-bug-demo/ and install dependencies.
2. `pnpm run dev`
3. Visit the server in a browser
4. See `ReferenceError: require is not defined`
5. Note that replacing step 2 with `pnpm run build && pnpm run preview` works fine.

title: Importing public files with `/* @vite-ignore */` dynamic imports throws an error
body:
### Description

My project generates JavaScript templates for non-technical users.  Before Vite, I published a zip file that looked like this:

- index.html
- config.js
- bundles/
  - mount.js

I'm trying to port this project to Vite.

To prevent Vite from minifying the source and mangling the name, I've tried putting `config.js` in `public`.  However, when I run `vite serve`, I'm met with this error message:

```
Failed to load url /config.js (resolved id: /config.js). This file is in /public and will be copied 
as-is during build without going through the plugin transforms, and therefore should not be 
imported from source code. It can only be referenced via HTML tags.
```

[Reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-ky9uhk?file=public%2Fsecret-number.js,main.js&terminal=dev)

While I respect the effort to prevent people from making mistakes, there ought to be the ability to say "no really, this is on purpose."

**In short, I want to be able to tell Vite _"Treat this JS file like any other asset.  Don't change its name or its contents, and allow it to be imported from the devserver."_**

### Suggested solution

The easiest solution from both an implementation and a user's POV would be a config flag, like `server.allowDangerousPublicDirImports`.  If it's set, Vite skips throwing the error and serves the requested file as if it's any other asset.

This gives the user the final decision about what is and is not permissible in their architecture, without resorting to crazy backdoors like writing a plugin to serve JS as an `assetInclude`.

The term `Dangerous` in the flag name warns people to not set it without consideration.  Using a flag gives it an obvious place to live in the documentation to make it easier for people to find.  (A nod could also be included in `ERR_LOAD_PUBLIC_URL`.) I'm not convinced that the risk of serving files from `publicDir` is so high that they need to individually be whitelisted.

### Alternative

Whitelisting, either by:

1. an inline comment, like `import(/* vite-treat-as-asset */ 'config.js)`, or
2. a config field, like `jsModulesInPublicDir: ['**/*config.js']`.

The comment is less discoverable than a config field, but easier to use.  You explicitly grant permission at the call site, so there is nothing to maintain.  (Imagine if the file name changes.)

A config field is DRYer (for instance, if many packages in a monorepo share a `vite.config`, one setting repairs the whole project).

### Additional context

`config.js` is effectively a JSON with generous commenting and some dependency injection to provide functionality like shuffling and centering.  

It's designed to be hand-edited by people who aren't technical enough to create or maintain a web app, but are capable of editing some strings.  All the complexity is in `mount.js`, which is just a blob to them.  They can edit the config file, drag it to a file server, and have an app that meets their needs without touching the command line.  Moreover, `config` can be generated by a web app after `mount` has already been minted.

title: `mergeConfig` doesn't merge `null` or `undefined` values
body:
### Describe the bug

When using `mergeConfig`, it is impossible to merge `null` or `undefined` values into the base config.

I've encountered this while using Remix ≥ 2.14.0, where `vite.mergeConfig` is used to merge a value for `server.watch` into the base config. This doesn't work for `null` or `undefined` values, which are the only two values Remix tries to merge.
(See [here](https://github.com/remix-run/remix/blob/remix%402.14.0/packages/remix-dev/vite/vite-node.ts#L21) for the `mergeConfig` call and [here](https://github.com/remix-run/remix/blob/remix%402.14.0/packages/remix-dev/vite/plugin.ts#L1053) for the data that's passed into it).
This results in the `server.watch` value never actually being set to anything in the final config, which in turn leads to a whole bunch of files being watched by vite that don't actually need watching during a build.

I'm not sure what the rationale was for [excluding `null` and `undefined` values](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts#L1171) when merging values, but I do see some use-cases for allowing them to be merged, like how remix tries (and fails) to do it.

Without additional context, I would expect any values in the `overrides` record to overwrite the `default` value, no matter what its value is. If I don't want to override a value, I shouldn't include its key in the `overrides` in the first place, so even `undefined` shouldn't receive special treatment as far as I'm concerned.

I've not submitted a PR because I'm not sure what other unforeseen side-effects the removal of that check would have.

I'd also be fine with keeping the check as-is, but then at the very least this quirk should be included in the [documentation](https://vite.dev/guide/api-javascript.html#mergeconfig).

title: `ssrLoadModule` errors on non-npm packages
body:
### Describe the bug

When using `ssrLoadModule` there is a hard coded assumption that any bare specifier would refer to an npm package. This is not true for runtimes like Deno which support more module formats. A bare specifier could refer to an npm package, a JSR package or even be a mapped local file.

The problematic code in question is here: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/0021527ccffcbf9baf447e6d111a8a7210750ebe/packages/vite/src/node/ssr/fetchModule.ts#L46-L78

title: Proxy: SSE connection abortion by server is not forwarded to clients
body:
### Describe the bug

This is similar to #13522, but for cases where the server aborts the connection.

When using SSE together with Vite as reverse proxy and the SSE response is aborted from the server side (e.g. server crash), the response channel to the client is not closed and the client has no idea that the server is gone, it just doesn't receive any data anymore.

The following code is my solution for this problem: Listen for `close` events on `proxyRes` (the response received from the proxied server) and if is aborted/errored **and** the client response hasn't been closed yet, destroy the client response.
The second condition is necessary because close events from the client side also trigger abnormal close events on `proxyRes` due to #13578
```ts
proxy.on("proxyRes", (proxyRes, req, res) => {
  proxyRes.on("close", () => {
    if (proxyRes.errored && !res.closed) {
      console.warn(`Proxy response for ${req.url} aborted, destroying client response`)
      res.destroy(proxyRes.errored)
    }
  })
})
```
_Note:_ Using `proxyRes.readableAborted` instead of `proxyRes.errored` should be equivalent, but would require a null/undefined corversion is `res.destroy`. Not sure if that's better or worse.

### Reproduction

not required?

### Steps to reproduce

1. use Vite as reverse proxy for a server providing an SSE (Event Stream) endpoint
2. from any browser, call the proxy SSE endpoint
3. kill the server
4. observe that the client doesn't receive any event

title: Unexpected naming of output chunks when using `cssCodeSplit`
body:
### Describe the bug

I am working on a project  where we have a number of entry points which import a mix of JS and CSS files. Some files are shared, others are not.

Where two different entry points include the same JavaScript and CSS files, the naming of the output chunks is not what I would expect it to be.

As an example:

```ts
// index.ts
import './index.css';

import './some-css.css';
import './some-js.ts';
```

```ts
// index-2.ts
import './index-2.css';

import './some-js.ts';
import './some-css.css';
```

gives the following files:
```
vite v7.1.5 building for production...
✓ 6 modules transformed.
dist/assets/entry-1.css  0.03 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/assets/entry-2.css  0.03 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/assets/some-js.css  0.10 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/my-app-entry-1.js   0.03 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/my-app-entry-2.js   0.03 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/shared-chunk.js     0.05 kB │ gzip: 0.07 kB
✓ built in 59ms
```
The unexpected aspect of  this is that it's emitted the contents of `some-css.css` as `some-js.css`

I would expect either:
- `some-js.js` would be emitted with the JS contents and `some-css.css` is emitted with the CSS content, OR
- both files have some shared name related to the file that is importing them, rather than the files being imported.

NOTE: in my real use-case the file names are completely different as the JS and CSS aren't closely related, they just both happen to be imported from the same pair of files. The above is just an example. 

I did some debugging and I think the Vite CSS plugin is allowing Rollup to generate a name for the Chunk, but Rollup can't come up with a good name so it falls back to the name of the last file imported (you can see this in action if you swap the order of the imports in the example). Ideally the plugin would pass a Chunk with just the JS imports to the JS processing and then another chunk with just the CSS imports. It might also be beneficial to give each chunk a name.

Another somewhat related issue is that the CSS asset being output doesn't receive the `originalFileNames` when using a `assetFileNames`/`chunkFileNames` callback which is interfering with my workflow for prefixing the file names with a certain subdirectory from the original file names, but it also prevents working around this issue by using the callbacks to override the name. This appears to be caused by the CSS chunk hardcoding an empty list of original files. If the plugin were to complete all of the metadata for the Chunk it would most likely solve both of these issues.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/jetwiwo/vite-repro-css-js-naming-issue

body:
### Describe the bug

Hi there!

In the latest version of my [rollup-plugin-node-externals](https://github.com/Septh/rollup-plugin-node-externals) plugin, the plugin factory is `async` and thus returns a `Promise`. title: Allow replacing environment variables after build
body:
### Description

Vite uses [production replacement](https://vitejs.dev/guide/env-and-mode.html#production-replacement) when handling the environment variables for an application being built in production mode. However, this means that it's impossible to alter the values after the build process. A main part of the benefit of containerized applications is that the same image can be used in multiple environments, but if the environment variables are baked into the compilation, this becomes impossible.

### Suggested solution

One possible solution is to allow the environment variables to instead be compiled into a JS/JSON file that can be altered after the build. This means that the container can write variables into that file during initialization, still allowing the application to be served statically (e.g. via Nginx).

This would probably mean that `import.meta.env` needs to be replaced with something else, like an include of the JSON file.

For example, this:
```typescript
location.href = import.meta.env.APP_ROOT_URL;
```

would become this:
```typescript
import metaEnv from '/env.json' assert {type: 'json'};
location.href = metaEnv.APP_ROOT_URL;
```

As long as this imported env.json file is rewritten by the container before serving starts, Nginx will be able to serve the app correctly.

### Alternative

The main alternative I see is for users to abandon the `import.meta.env` functionality so that they can provide this flexibility themselves. We're figuring out how to do this for our app already.

title: Add dev server route to resolve entries by name
body:
### Description

When integrating Vite with a backend, it is currently cumbersome to reference entry points via their name specified in `build.rollupOptions.input` during development. In production, it's easy thanks to the manifest file, but there is currently no counterpart during development.

Picture the following scenario:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  base: '/static/', // this makes it even more fuzzy
  build: {
    manifest: true,
    rollupOptions: {
      input: {
        main: './frontend/js/main.ts',
        exampleForm: './frontend/js/forms/example.ts',
        nestedDependency: './node_modules/mymodule/process-me.ts' // probably not best practice, but sometimes reality
      }
    },
  },
})
```

Currently, you have to specify the path in the URL of the script to include the assets.

```html
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@vite/client"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/static/frontend/js/main.ts"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/static/frontend/js/forms/example.ts"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/static/node_modules/mymodule/process-me.ts"></script>
```

### Suggested solution

While the above way works, it'd be nicer to be able to reference the entries by their specified name:


```html
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@vite/client"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@entry/main"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@entry/exampleForm"></script>
<script type="module" src="http://localhost:5173/@entry/nestedDependency"></script>
```

The dev server would simply resolve the entry by its name and redirect accordingly (`http://localhost:5173/@entry/main` → 302 `http://localhost:5173/static/frontend/js/main.ts`)

When moving files around, one would only have to update the Vite config, instead of potentially many references.

### Alternative

- Using plugins such as https://github.com/owlsdepartment/vite-plugin-dev-manifest
- Creating a new third-party plugin which adds the proposed `@entry` routes to the dev server

### Additional context

We're using `django-vite` and have many such lines in our codebase:

```django
{% vite_asset 'frontend/js/forms/example-form.ts' %}
```

This seems much more maintainable to me (but doesn't currently work during development, as it's not possible to get the asset's path from its name):

```django
{% vite_asset 'exampleForm' %}
```

title: `ModuleRunner` - Sharing `concurrentModuleNodePromises` across invocations is not compatible with Cloudflare Workers runtime
body:
### Describe the bug

The caching of `concurrentModuleNodePromises` implemented in the `ModuleRunner` is not compatible with the Cloudflare Workers runtime.

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/ec067671d019023109f974310a9cd974a4091251/packages/vite/src/module-runner/runner.ts#L233-L251

This is because it violates a constraint of the Workers runtime that I/O objects can't be shared between invocations (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/errors/#cannot-perform-io-on-behalf-of-a-different-request). We have only encountered this recently when debugging https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/9518 but it seems to be a common issue for users building larger apps.

It would be good to understand if this promise caching is just an optimisation or if it serves to prevent invalid states. If it's just an optimisation then the simplest option might be to offer a way to opt out.

SSR transformed named imported functions don't work with debuggers "step-into"
body:
### Describe the bug

Originally reported at https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/5569. I think I've seen 2-3 similar reports in the past too.

When a file is SSR transformed in Vite, debuggers like Chrome Dev tools and VSCode are unable to ["step into"](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/javascript/reference#step-into) functions that are imported via named imports. In practice this means stopping debugger in line 3 and pressing "step into" button of debuggers in the example below.

```ts
1 | import { add } from "./math.ts";
2 |
3 | add(1, 2);
```

Debugger should stop at line 1 or 2, but instead it stops at 7.

```ts
1 | export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
2 |   if (a === 1) {
3 |     return 1;
4 |   }
5 | 
6 |   return a + b;
7 | }
8 |
```

Source map of the `math.ts` in reproduction: [https://evanw.github.io/source-map-visualization/#NDI2AGZ1bmN0...](https://evanw.github.io/source-map-visualization/#).

<details>
  <summary>Video demonstrating step-into issue with Vite SSR</summary>

[vite-step-into.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dcd19667-b3f1-4689-af22-9875a8aba675)

</details>

I think this has something to do with the way Vite SSR transforms `import` into `import()` and saves the results into single variable. In the reproduction setup I've created "Vite simulation", where SSR transformed file is loaded directly into Node. 

In this example "step into" works correctly on lines 11 and 15. If Vite was able to destructure the named imports of `__vite_ssr_exports__` into separate variables, I think debuggers would work just fine. But this would break ESM live bindings. 

```ts
 1 | globalThis.__vite_ssr_exports__ = {};
 2 | debugger;
 3 | 
 4 | await import("./transpiled.js");
 5 | const { add, multiply } = globalThis.__vite_ssr_exports__;
 6 | 
 7 | // Incorrect position when "step into"
 8 | globalThis.__vite_ssr_exports__.add(1, 2);
 9 | 
10 | // Correct position when "stepinto"
11 | add(1, 2);
12 | 
13 | // Same here
14 | globalThis.__vite_ssr_exports__.multiply(1, 2);
15 | multiply(1, 2);
16 |
```

<details>
  <summary>Video showing how lines 11 and 15 work correctly</summary>

[node-step-into.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4cf99eb6-6abb-4fcc-9af3-c7f84befce05)

</details>

title: history 模式下 vite.config.js 配置 base: './' 路由跳转后无法正确获取到对应 js 、css 文件
body:
### Describe the bug

在使用 `pnpm create vue@latest` 搭建的项目后，`vite.config.ts` 配置的 `base:'./'`  然后打包后放在服务器上部署，nginx 配置: 
```
location /test {
            alias  html/dist;
            try_files $uri $uri/ /test/index.html;
            index  index.html index.htm;
        }
```

在启动 nginx 后访问   www.demo.com/test  首页能够正常访问，但是涉及到 `vue-router` 跳转后就无法正确访问到了。
比如在项目中 配置了 /home  和 /login  两个路由，当访问 www.demo.com/test/home 时页面无法正确访问，打开浏览器发现请求的js 路径是 `www.demo.com/test/home/js/index-CrKRtstp.js`  而正确的文件路径应该是  `www.demo.com/test/js/index-CrKRtstp.js`。

在项目中我是用 `base: './'` 这样配置的原因是在前端打包后会在同一个服务器上根据路径不同 部署不同环境的前端项目。比如：`www.demo.com/test` 和 `www.demo.com/dev`  分别访问的是 测试环境和 开发环境的前端项目。

title: Allow HTML to live in a subdirectory of the project
body:
### Description

If I'm building an MPA, the top-level of my project ends up being a mix of:

- `index.html` the entry point
- `foo/index.html` another entry point
- `vite.config.ts`
- `lib/*.ts` some project specific plugins
- `public`

…and it feels a bit of a mix. I'd like to be able to put the build entrypoints in their own directory, such as `src`, but I don't want a `src` directory to appear in `dist`.

Changing `root` means you have to then change `public` and a bunch of other stuff, to move them a directory up. It also doesn't seem to play well with other plugins.

### Suggested solution

An option like `entryRoot`, which specifies the root for build entry points.

title: [HMR] TailwindCSS do not compile new CSS when files with HMR changed
body:
### Describe the bug

TailwindCSS does not compile new CSS when a file is modified and handled by HMR (e.g. a Vue SFC) in dev mode.

The class name of the element is updated by the Vue plugin via HMR, but Tailwind doesn't create a new rule for the new class name. So the new class name becomes useless.

There is a similar issue, which is about pug: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/4588

And there is also a relative test (pug only): https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-vue/blob/main/playground/tailwind/__tests__/tailwind.spec.ts.

I think it is an issue of Vite, not plugin-vue. Because this also happens to my web framework and its plugin (with HMR).

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-8djtq2?file=src%2FApp.vue

### Steps to reproduce

1. `install` and `dev`
2. The text "test" in the preview panel is blue
3. modify `App.vue`: `text-blue-400`→`text-red-400`
4. The text "test" becomes black, instead of red, which means the `.text-red-400` rule is not generated.

It's bug in [http-proxy](https://github.com/http-party/node-http-proxy/issues/1706)

title: Blocks path although server proxy applies
body:
### Describe the bug

I am building a client for my file server and need to serve the same index.html for almost every path. Precisely, I am using `server.proxy` to map each path matching `"/D:*"` to `"/"` via `vite.config.ts` like this:

```ts
import {defineConfig} from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
    // ... other options
    server: {
        proxy: {
            "/D:*": "/"
        }
    }
});
```

This is not unique to this folder; any path **that exists** is getting blocked, while paths that are not found just resolve to `"/"`. This should not happen since the URL is getting remapped.

title: Improve Handling When Resolving URLs Wildcard Certificates in extractHostnamesFromSubjectAltName
body:
### Describe the bug

When you specify a certificate using `server.https.cert` in your `vite.config.ts`, we attempt to use the SubjectAltName from the provided cert to suggest additional resolved names.

On my home network, I use a wildcard certificate `*.bren.haus`, to allow all of my devices to serve HTTPS traffic to each other, and I have configured each of my devices to resolve to a subdomain of that domain.

However, when trying to resolve URLs for a wildcard cert, Vite will always pick `vite` as the subdomain. 

[`extractHostnamesFromSubjectAltName`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts#L1068)
```ts
if (
      name === 'DNS' &&
      // [::1] might be included but skip it as it's already included as a local address
      value !== '[::1]' &&
      // skip *.IPv4 addresses, which is invalid
      !(value.startsWith('*.') && net.isIPv4(value.slice(2)))
    ) {
      hostnames.push(value.replace('*', 'vite'))
    }
``` 

I don't currently resolve `vite.bren.haus`, so I would love to be able to configure this value in some way. The reason I specifically care about properly resolving the URL is that I have a plugin that depends on it.


### Reproduction

https://github.com/brenapp/referee.fyi

### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate a Wildcard Certificate
2. Specify the certificate in your vite config
3. Incorrectly assumes vite subdomain

title: HMR does not update the content when using react and there's a circular import
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi, multiple members of the team I'm working in are suffering from Vite's HMR sometimes not working at all (not even full page reloads happen, the page just isn't updated). In some files in the codebase, it consistently never works.

We're using vite together with react. It's driving us crazy when it doesn't work, since we've gotten used to HMR always working, so when things don't behave as expected in the browser, we first think our code is at fault. We re-think approaches and add debug information, only to notice even that doesn't work. Then we reload the page, which unfortunately given our project size takes around 35 seconds (so it isn't a viable workaround to always reload). After a reload, our code suddenly works, and we get frustrated.

This led me to providing this reproduction, in hopes of someone knowing how to fix it. As copying files into a fresh repo didn't reproduce the bug, I have started out with the file where HMR never worked for us (`useAnimationStyling`) and spent hours painstakingly deleting files from our project.

Unfortunately, the "hit rate" of the bug has gone down from 100% to ~15% in the process, yet the "minimal" reproduction contains 45 files. Most of them just contain one import and one export though.

Apparently, the bug has at least something to do with project size, as deleting a bunch of unused files (not imported at all from vite's entrypoint) from our actual repo seems to have decreased the success rate down to matching the one of the attached reproduction repo.

Please have some patience when trying to follow the reproduction steps.

Related issue: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/16284 but I don't think this is the same since for us it works for some files all the time and never for some others.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/danieltroger/vite-hmr-bug-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. `git clone https://github.com/danieltroger/vite-hmr-bug-repro`
2. `cd vite-hmr-bug-repro`

title: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module
body:
### Describe the bug

Since switching to Vite we noticed a new production issue, where sometimes users are encountering an error if we deploy while they have an active session:

> **TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module**

I believe this is because if any code is modified in an area that Vite would turn into a dynamic module, then the file hash changes, however when they try to visit an area that would trigger the dynamic load, those files no longer exist so they hit the error message above. 

Quoting from https://stackoverflow.com/a/74057337/21061
> When you dynamically import a route/component, during build it creates a separate chunk. By default, chunk filenames are hashed according to their content – Overview.abc123.js. If you don't change the component code, the hash remains the same. If the component code changes, the hash changes too - Overview.32ab1c.js. This is great for caching.
> 
> Now this is what happens when you get this error:
>
> - You deploy the application
> - Your Home chunk has a link to /overview route, which would load Overview.abc123.js
> - Client visits your site
> - You make changes in your code, not necessarily to the Overview component itself, but maybe to some children components that Overview imports.
> - You deploy changes, and Overview is built with a different hash now - Overview.32ab1c.js
> - Client clicks on /overview link - gets the Failed to fetch dynamically imported module error, because Overview.abc123.js no longer exists
>
> That is why the errors correlate with deployments. One way to fix it is to not use lazy loaded routes, but that's not a great solution when you have many heavy routes - it will make your main bundle large

What I expect to happen, is not to encounter any errors if the users session remains active during a deployment.

I have been unable to come up with a good workaround (specifically for me using React ErrorBoundary is the best I can do so far with a re-direct similar to https://stackoverflow.com/a/74861436/21061 which is a mitigation and provides quite a poor user experience flashing an error message).

### Reproduction

https://github.com/IPWright83/vite-dynamic-import

### Steps to reproduce

The above repository has been set up to **mimick** a production deployment as obviously that is a much more complicated set-up. It leverages `React.lazy` to force a dynamic module and uses a `setTimeout` to provide a delay with which to simulate a user navigation to a page requiring a module. In a real production scenario I don't believe `React.lazy` is required.

- Clone the above repository
- npm install
- npm run build
- open a 2nd terminal

- **Terminal 1** npx serve dist (starts a web server)
- **Browser** open the URL (usually localhost:3000)
- **Text Editor** modify src/Foo.jsx changing the string "Foo" to something else (within 30s of launching the page - increase the setTimeout in App.jsx if this is not long enough)
- **Terminal 2** npm run build

Wait... 30s after loading the page you should see a blank page render with errors in the browser console:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1374775/214322173-001e2852-9d13-49ea-a47f-a01fd4e4558f.png)

If you were to reload the page, you can see that `Foo-b53985a6.js` has been renamed to `Foo-535d5a10.js` (or similar new hash)

### System Info

```shell
❯ npx envinfo --system --npmPackages '{vite,@vitejs/*}' --binaries --browsers

    OS: Linux 5.15 Ubuntu 20.04.5 LTS (Focal Fossa)

```
```

title: Importing resource with URL no longer bundles the asset (>=7.1.0 regression)
body:
### Describe the bug

A standard integration of [react-pdf](https://github.com/wojtekmaj/react-pdf) with [pdfjs-dist](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js) as described in their documentation works correctly with vite 7.0.6 and older but not with 7.1.0 or newer.

Given the following minimal example of react-pdf:

```js
import { pdfjs } from 'react-pdf'

pdfjs.GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc = new URL(
  'pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs',
  import.meta.url,
).toString()
```

With vite 7.0.6 or older the `pdf.worker.min.mjs` asset is correctly bundled and present in the dist directory:
```
dist/assets/pdf.worker.min--PgD6g2g.mjs              1,035.02 kB

title: pre-bundle all dependencies ahead of time (for dev mode)
body:
### Description

I'm using Vitest with Playwright, and pre-bundling during tests causes issues. Tests seems to fail when something like the following happens:

```
11:37:14 AM [vite] (client) ✨ new dependencies optimized: @shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/option/option.js, @shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/tag/tag.js, lit/directives/live.js, @shoelace-style/shoelace/dist/components/popup/popup.js
11:37:14 AM [vite] (client) ✨ optimized dependencies changed. reloading

[vitest] Vite unexpectedly reloaded a test. This may cause tests to fail, lead to flaky behaviour or duplicated test runs.
For a stable experience, please add mentioned dependencies to your config's `optimizeDeps.include` field manually.
```

which seems to cause tests to fail like so:

```
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Suites 3 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯

Caused by: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:63315/home/docker/app/components/dist/drop-down.test.js?import&browserv=1755229233394
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯[1/2]⎯

title: add an option to not to inline assets in library mode when format is 'es'
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Currently when using library mode, all the assets (images, videos...) are inlined using base64. When those assets are big, it takes a long for vite to build, and the browser also takes a long time to parse the javascript.

### Suggested solution

When the library format is 'es', we can add an option to make vite emit those files, and import those files in javascript using `new URL(import.meta.url, '...')`, e.g. 

```javascript
import foo from './image.png';

const bar = foo; // new URL(import.meta.url, './assets/image.2d8efhg.png')
```

title: double deps creation causes dev fail on Windows under Netlify vite-plugin
body:
### Describe the bug At suggestion of Netlfiy Support, I'm reporting here also as I have to their repo involving this. It's Vite's new activity of staging deps creation which cases an EPERM crash of run dev when on Windows. The trail of this is using @astrojs/netlify adapter in an Astro project at @6.5.0 and plus, which encorporates Netlify's viite-plugin. The following is the full report given there, which includes a minimal reproduction, a workaround which temporarily but not satisfactorily allows work, and a screenshot showing what to expect when the minimal reproduction functions instead of crashing out with the EPERM -- you'll need that. Justification for fixing this is explained in the preface to [the netlify reop issue here](https://github.com/netlify/primitives/issues/408), I think...thanks.... Mainly, the Vite config 'workaround' is both awkward and demanding, even if 'simple' once arrived at -- not at all the sort of thing either Netlify or especially Astro(-Sanity) designer-developers will be able to or should be asked to deal with. As you are no doubt aware, Vite is mystery meat in those contexts. So, thanks again. The reproduction necessarily involves the large chunk of Sanity module which excites it, but you won't have to deal with that in any way except to click the link that attempts its first stages. Note that proper operation also gives an error, due to truncation to minimal everything, but that's clear, on-screen instead of in console, and that I've provided a screenshot to show how it looks. ### Reproduction https://github.com/narration-sd/astro-netlify-sanity ### Steps to reproduce - use these steps with the minimal repo cloned -- ***being sure to the N.B. at the botttom of this section!!!***: - run it using npm install, then npm run dev, then clicking the dev link to show a minimal html page - click the link on the page to attempt opening the Studio - you will get a persistent blank page, and after some extended seconds, the dev console will show an EPERM error from Vite attempting to substitute in an expanded node_modules/.vite/deps, but failing, as you can observe by looking there. That's the fault. After conversation with Netlify support, a workaround was arrived at, force-including all modules used by the Studio via Vite config in the astro.config.mjs: ``` integrations: [ ... ], vite: { optimizeDeps: { force: true, include: [ 'sanity/**/*', // list further all that are includes in a real sanity.config.ts ], }, }, adapter: netlify() ``` This is sufficient for the minimal demo, and works when extended to include all modules used in a real site Studio's sanity.config.ts. Which is awkward, but does function for proving. When you add the workaround config to the minimal tester, then clicking the Studio link will give a properly expected error that there is no projectId specified, as in this screenshot; and there will be no EPERM showing in the dev console. When a fully configured Studio is tested, it simply operates correctly once the special Vite config has been added, demonstrating all complex visual editing etc. operations. Screenshot of properly working minmal demo's expected error: N.B. PLEASE BE VERY THOUGHTFUL HERE!!! ...if you have done the above, run and seen the EPERM fail, then added the 'workaround' to see the screenshot result which is proper operation for this minimal reproduction.... ...then you ***must*** afterwards completely remove node_modules/.vite folder before testing in any way for the EPERM fail again. Otherwise Vite will see a fully constructed deps, and not exercise its double dep building which causes (on Windows) the fail.... Of course you must do this every time, in developing a fix. ### System Info ```shell System: OS: Windows 11 10.0.26100 CPU: (16) x64 AMD Ryzen 7 6800H with Radeon Graphics Memory: 19.51 GB / 39.19 GB Binaries: Node: 24.4.1 - ~\AppData\Local\Volta\tools\image\node\24.4.1\node.EXE npm: 11.4.2 - ~\AppData\Local\Volta\tools\image\node\24.4.1\npm.CMD pnpm: 10.12.1 - C:\Program Files\Volta\pnpm.EXE bun: 1.2.18 - ~\scoop\shims\bun.EXE Browsers: Edge: Chromium (139.0.3405.86) Internet Explorer: 11.0.26100.1882 n.b. this is a bit wack, as a) I never touch Edge b) I'm not using Chrome in any form for development; rather clean basis latest Firefox c) browser is not involved with this problem. ``` ### Used Package Manager npm ### Logs

title: We decided to release the [Environment API branch](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16471) as `vite@6.0.0-alpha.x` (we'll continue regularly releasing new alpha patches).
body:
We decided to release the [Environment API branch](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16471) as `vite@6.0.0-alpha.x` (we'll continue regularly releasing new alpha patches).

The changes started by the [Runtime API]https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/ddos/what-is-a-ddos-attack/(https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/15774) are now prompting a complete review of the way Vite handles environments (client, SSR, workerd, etc). We were originally going to release this branch as `vite@5.3.0-alpha.0` but the changes are now too big for a minor so we're going to start working on the next major directly with it. We're probably going to have ~2 months of alpha period and once we feel confident with the stability of the new APIs, we'll kick the beta.

If you are building a framework or are working in a Runtime (like the Cloudflare team), the next months are going to be very important to get the APIs right and serve as the base for the next iteration. We're thinking on lifting Vite's responsibilities to be able to share more in the ecosystem. For example, we're introducing the concept of a `ViteBuilder` that lets frameworks orchestrate all the environment builds they need to get a single `vite build` command to build the whole app. This means changing our stance on the "framework-as-a-plugin" pattern (SvelteKit, Remix, QwikCity, etc), and making it a first class pattern from Vite 6 forward.

Check out the current [Environment API docs](https://deploy-preview-16471--vite-docs-main.netlify.app/guide/api-vite-environment.html) and give us feedback. This discussion is a good place to gather it, please share your impressions and PoCs as you test.

If you think someone you know would be interested in helping us testing and creating prototypes (Workerd framework-agnostic integrations, RSC, etc), please contact them so they can get involved.

Resources:

- [Environment API PR](github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16471)
- [Environment API Docs](https://deploy-preview-16471--vite-docs-main.netlify.app/guide/api-vite-environment.html)

Previous discussions:

- [Runtime API PR](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/12165)
- [Runtime API Feedback discussion](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/15774)
- [Initial Docs PR](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16089)
- [Initial Implementation PR](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/16129)

History:

Check out @antfu's [Dev SSR on Nuxt post](https://antfu.me/posts/dev-ssr-on-nuxt), explaining @pi0's [Dev Bundler idea](https://github.com/nuxt/vite/pull/201) that led to the creation of [vite-node](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/tree/main/packages/vite-node#readme). Anthony used vite-node to as the engine of [Vitest](https://vitest.dev). After revamping it, @sheremet-va added a revised version of [vite-node in Vite Core](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/12165) in Vite 5.1. The Environment API is a new iteration, deeply integrating the features vite-node provided in Vite's API.

_Originally posted by @patak-dev in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/16358_

title: Vite produces invalid output paths when rebasing URLs in SCSS files
body:
### Describe the bug

I have a Vite.js application where I import an SCSS file from a dependency. In a CSS bundle produce by Vite, the path is incorrect and invalid.

This issue seems to be specific to the file structure, as I can reproduce it if the SCSS file name matches the target directory name except the leading underscore and the `url()` argument is built using a variable:

```
├── foobar
│   └── static.png
└──  _foobar.scss // <- url("foobar/#{$file-name}.png")
```

In the resulting bundle, the `foobar/static.png` relative path is rebased to become `.../xxx/_foobar.scssstatic.png` (see the reproduction repo).

In the real life scenario, although we do control the said dependency, changes to its file structure constitute a breaking change for our customers, that is why it's important for us that this issue is addressed.

This issue may look a bit similar to the existing scss path rebase issues, both fixed and active (https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/11012, https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/19058), but I believe it may be a separate problem given that the open issues do not mention distorted file paths.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/VasilyStrelyaev/vite-scss-path-rebase-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run build` to build a barebone app in `packages/client-app`
3. Open the build output at `packages/client-app/dist/assets/index-XXX.css`
4. Search for the `url()` function and notice its argument. Vite rebased the `foobar/react.png` relative path so that it became invalid: `../../scss-dep/src/_foobar.scssreact.png`

title: Share chunk across the main bundle and web worker bundle
body:
### Describe the bug

Please refer to this repository for a way to reproduce the issue: https://github.com/gabrielecirulli/vite-pixi-bundling

When bundling Web Worker code with Vite, some of the dependencies that are used
by both the worker and the page context are duplicated in the final bundle, even
though they should be shared because they are virtually the same code.

In the provided repository, `pixi.js` is used to render to two instances of `canvas`, once within the page context and once within a Web Worker.

To do this, we have a file `canvas.ts` which imports `pixi.js` and exports a class called `Canvas`. We also have a `worker.ts` script that will run as a web worker. Both the worker script and `main.ts` import the `Canvas` class and set it up. Other than this they virtually do the same thing.

Intuitively, all of `pixi.js` should just be bundled once and shared across the two page context and web worker scripts which import it. However, the code ends up duplicated and bloating the bundle size (see build logs)

As far as I can tell, there is nothing in the Vite or Rollup docs that helps with this. I have tried various combinations of `manualChunks` and other options to no avail.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/gabrielecirulli/vite-pixi-bundling

### Steps to reproduce

- Clone [this repository](https://github.com/gabrielecirulli/vite-pixi-bundling)
- Run `pnpm install`
- Run `pnpm run build`
- Check the generated modules in `dist/assets`


## Comparing the build output
[The repository](https://github.com/gabrielecirulli/vite-pixi-bundling) includes a branch called `with-manual-chunks`.  This branch forces Rollup to bundle all code belonging to `pixi.js` into a manual chunk called `pixi.js`. This way, you can compare the two bundles to see the (lack of) differences:

- Switch to branch `with-manual-chunks`
- Run `pnpm install`
- Run `pnpm run build`

title: Vite plugin transform function needs the source map of the input if it was transformed by another module.
body:
### Description

I'm currently writing a vite plugin that transforms the source code in some way. Critically, this transformation involves file and line numbers of the source file.

If the source file has already been processed by another plugin (for instance the react plugin has already processed JSX) then the files and line emitted are erroneous because, as far as I know, the source map of the previous transform is not available.

If there is already a way to do this that I missed, please point me to it. I'm relatively new to Vite and could definitively have missed it. However, my current research leads me to think the previous source map is not available.

### Suggested solution

Update the transform API to add an "options" parameter that is a map of things that could be passed down to plugins, such as the map generated by a previous plugin if there is one. While the doc does not mention such a field, it seems to already exists in an undocumented state, and the source map of previous transform could be provided there.

### Alternative

The alternative is to generate erroneous file/line numbers when a previous transform is involved. The good is that it doesn't require to do anything, but the bad is that it looks clowny and makes for poor debug experience.

title: Support Development Build Output (write files to disk during vite dev for Code Federation
body:
### Description

Currently, during vite dev, Vite serves modules from memory and does not emit real build files to disk.
This behavior is optimal for most cases, but it becomes a limitation when working with Code Federation (such as using [vite-plugin-federation](https://github.com/originjs/vite-plugin-federation)) or similar tools that need actual physical files to dynamically import modules across applications.

Because there are no real files, remote apps cannot resolve federation modules during development unless a full vite build (production) is run — which slows down the feedback cycle significantly.


### Why this is needed
For a smooth development experience with Vite Code Federation and future plugin ecosystems relying on actual file outputs, it would be very useful to have an optional development build mode that:

- Writes the dev server output files to disk (e.g., into dist-dev/)

- Retains fast dev server behavior (no minification, fast rebuilds)

- Makes it possible for remote modules to be dynamically loaded without needing a production build

This improves developer experience for microfrontends, code federation, and complex dynamic module scenarios.



### Suggested solution

Introduce a new optional config field:

```js
// vite.config.ts
export default {
  build: {
    devBuildToDisk: true, // default: false
  },
}
```

Behavior:

- When enabled, during vite dev, after each Rollup bundle update, output the generated chunks into a designated folder (dist-dev/ or configurable).

- No minification, keep sourcemaps optional.

- Fast HMR and live reload behavior is retained.

- Plugins like vite-plugin-federation can directly use these files.



### Alternative

- Running vite build --watch: however, this triggers production optimizations (minification, tree-shaking) which slows down dev workflow.

- Creating a custom plugin: but it would be better if Vite provides native support, to standardize and improve the federation/microfrontend ecosystem.

### Additional context

Some existing plugin ecosystems (e.g., vite-plugin-federation) have workarounds to simulate build outputs, but a clean first-party solution would be more maintainable and developer-friendly.

Implementing this would open doors for better dynamic module loading support during development and encourage wider adoption of Vite for microfrontend architectures.

title: Support devtools project settings
body:
### Description

Google Chrome added a feature for [automatic workspace folders](https://chromium.googlesource.com/devtools/devtools-frontend/+/main/docs/ecosystem/automatic_workspace_folders.md) detection. On localhost URLs, Chrome requests `/.well-known/appspecific/com.chrome.devtools.json`. This endpoint must serve the following JSON:

```json
{
  "workspace": {
    "root": "/path/to/project/root",
    "uuid": "6ec0bd7f-11c0-43da-975e-2a8ad9ebae0b"
  }
}
```

This is kind of useful, but also annoying. Many servers don’t implement this, meaning the request yields 404 Not Found.

The Chrome team also made [`vite-plugin-devtools-json`](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/vite-plugin-devtools-json). This works well, but I expect most users won’t install a plugin just for this.

### Suggested solution

Incorporate this functionality into the Vite dev server by default.

### Alternative

Don’t add this functionality.

title: DOMException when using web worker during dev with backend integration
body:
### Describe the bug

I am trying to use web workers in order to not clog the main thread (when computing hashes of large files for instance).

We have a backend so I'm using some kind a backend integration in dev mode. As such, for the assets to load properly we're going the "origin" approach (i.e., forcing server.origin be https://localhost:5173 in the vite config). I won't be able to go the "proxy route" as suggested in the documentation due to network constraints.

Using this, the assets load but when using web workers, I encounter the following error:
~~~
Uncaught (in promise) DOMException: Failed to construct 'Worker': Script at 'https://localhost:5173/src/utils/hash.worker.js?type=module&worker_file' cannot be accessed from origin 'https://app-dev.net'.
    at new WorkerWrapper (https://localhost:5173/src/utils/hash.worker.js?worker&inline:2:18)
    at ttt (https://localhost:5173/src/main.js:144:20)
    at https://localhost:5173/src/main.js:148:1
~~~

I understand why that's the case, but I have no idea as to what I can do to make it work. I tried adding CSP headers to no avail.
I know this can be circumvented by using a Blob URL and a raw import, but the code inside the worker has to be transpiled in my case since I'm doing some import there.

Everything works fine when built, I noticed it uses the "Blob trick" too, on the transpiled source.

Is there a way to mimic this in dev mode?

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-hwpuck

### Steps to reproduce

You won't able to reproduce in stackblitz but you can by downloading the code to run it locally.
Open 2 terminals : one for vite and the other one for the backend.
In the vite terminal, run `npm install && npm run dev`
In the backend terminal, run `node server.js`
Access the backend (http://localhost:8000). In the browser console, you'll see the error.

### Describe the bug

We use less as css preprocessor. There we have a setup with mixins filling image-sets.

title: Documentation: Clarify limitations of `html.cspNonce` for SPA deployments.
body:
### Documentation is

- [x] Missing
- [ ] Outdated
- [x] Confusing
- [ ] Not sure?

### Explain in Detail

#### Update:

Thanks to the clarification from @sapphi-red, I now have a better understanding of the intended mechanism. My initial report had some incorrect assumptions:
1. I now understand the `<meta property="csp-nonce">` is for Vite's internal use, not for setting the policy itself.
2. I also understand that `html.cspNonce` should be set to a *literal placeholder string* (e.g., `'CSP_NONCE_PLACEHOLDER'`), not a randomly generated value within `vite.config.js`. This is correctly documented.

My core concern remains, however, that the documentation doesn't adequately guide the user on *how* to implement the required server-side replacement, especially in common deployment scenarios like SPAs, where it might interfere with caching. I've detailed this in my follow-up comment below, suggesting that maybe the docs should point to hash-based CSP as a better solution for the typical Vite user.


#### Original:

Hey there,

First off, thank you for building and maintaining Vite! 

As documented elsewhere, notably [here](https://vite-csp.tsotne.co.uk/guides/spa) and [here](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/16749), there might be some amount of perceived "security theater" on Vite's documentation regarding the **Content Security Policy (CSP)** info mentioned prominently on the ["Features" page](https://vite.dev/guide/features.html#content-security-policy-csp):

> ## Content Security Policy (CSP)
> 
> To deploy CSP, certain directives or configs must be set due to Vite's internals.
> 
> ### 'nonce-{RANDOM}'
>
> When `html.cspNonce` is set, Vite adds a nonce attribute with the specified value to any `<script>` and `<style>` tags, as well as `<link>` tags for stylesheets and module preloading. Additionally, when this option is set, Vite will inject a meta tag (`<meta property="csp-nonce" nonce="PLACEHOLDER" />`).
>
> The nonce value of a meta tag with `property="csp-nonce"` will be used by Vite whenever necessary during both dev and after build.
>
> WARNING: Ensure that you replace the placeholder with a unique value for each request. This is important to prevent bypassing a resource's policy, which can otherwise be easily done.

#### First of, a bit of a *CSP 101*:

- Basically, CSP is a set of security measures in which the server should send, for all resource URIs, a `Content-Security-Policy` header, containing some restrictions for the user argent to follow, regarding from which origins or URIs the user agent can load resources. 
  - It helps mitigate attacks like *Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)*
  - Examples: ``` Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' https://example.com; ```
  - The keyword `default-src` defines the basic policy, which can then be tuned for particular resource types, such as `script-src`.
  - The value `self` limits new resources to those with the same origin.
  - Typically, you would enable 'self', plus trusted origins such as CDNs.
- Also, the `nonce` mechanism is used to limit execution of inline scripts to those for which a corresponding `nonce` attribute is present on the script tag.
  - As the name implies, each response should contain an unique nonce.
  - Example:
    ```html
    <!-- Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' 'nonce-abc123'; -->
    <script nonce="abc123">console.log("Hello, world!");</script>
    <script>console.log("This will not run!");</script>
    ```
- The CSP information could be provided on a `<meta>` tag, but this is considered less secure than on the HTTP Header. [(source)](https://content-security-policy.com/examples/meta/)

#### Back to `html.cspNonce`

Now, the issues I find when trying to implement this feature are the following:
- The `meta` tag is not the right way to implement this. It should be done with a `Content-Security-Policy` HTTP header if possible [(source)](https://content-security-policy.com/examples/meta/)
- If you generate a random `nonce` both for the header and for the `html.cspNonce` option, on the `vite.config.js`, Vite would read this file twice at different times to generate one or the other, entirely breaking your site by not having a matching nonce everywhere.
- Even worse, if you build a SPA with `vite build`, the `nonce` will be generated only once, which is not secure at all, as it should be different for every request. Not to mention that `nonce` is not compatible with static content which is usually cached.
- Some partial measures exist, such as the plugin `vite-plugin-csp-guard`, but it notoriously documents that it *doesn't* generate a nonce for SPAs [(source)](https://vite-csp.tsotne.co.uk/guides/spa), rather relying on "hash-based CSP."

This discovery process can be frustrating and time-consuming. More importantly, a developer might miss the nuance and deploy a statically-generated `nonce`, creating a false sense of security. The fact that this is a known point of confusion is validated by existing issues linked above.

### Your Suggestion for Changes

I propose that the documentation for the `html.cspNonce` option be updated to explicitly state its limitations and current recomended usage (if any). Adding a prominent warning or tip would be incredibly effective.

Thank you again for your time and for all your hard work on Vite.

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

title: Unable to parse HTML; parse5 error code control-character-in-input-stream
body:
### Describe the bug

While trying to serve a HTML file generated by Turbowarp via Vite (which uses parse5) the parser complains on control characters, see https://github.com/TurboWarp/packager/issues/986.

The HTML file contains control characters as part of an embedded JavaScript Fragment, the are used to indicate parts of a Zip File header and several other internal strings. Opening such a generated file in a browser works without any issues.

After creating a issue agains TurboWaro (see above) I've created one against `parse5`, see https://github.com/inikulin/parse5/issues/1555
The outcome was that while this is reported as an error the severity of those parser errors should be considered to be a warning, see https://github.com/inikulin/parse5/issues/1555#issuecomment-3121996347

title: Vite can hang the node.js process if server is closed during file transform
body:
### Describe the bug

If `addWatchFile()` is called by a Vite plugin after the server is closed, the watcher will be set, preventing Node.js process from exiting.

For example, if vite:css was in the middle of transforming a file when the server is closed, vite:css may call `addWatchFile()` , which will hang the process.

   cd vite-app
