title: Disabling WebSocket and HMR
body:
### Description

Some users are actively seeking ways to disable HMR (#13994).

With HML enabled, and reactive components are partially rendered, it is unpredictable #18217 when page reload happens.
From my personal experience, the page reloads multiple times, even during simple navigation within the project.


### Suggested solution

Please provide an option for users to disable WebSocket and HMR.
```
    server: {
        socket: false,
        hmr: false,
    },
```
A single page reload after updating code in the editor is sufficient and might be optimal solution.
Fortunately, Vite is capable of updating CSS and JS files even without WebSocket enabled.

### Alternative

![Screenshot 2024-10-28 at 05 35 52](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdb732f3-614f-479f-870c-325c1a327fbb)


### Additional context

Normally I do not change the library's code. However, this changes made my developing experience much more predictable and less annoying with unexpected reloads.
```
function setupWebSocket(protocol, hostAndPath, onCloseWithoutOpen) {
  if (!socketEnabled) return;
```

Thanks.

import.meta.glob(["./modules/*.js", "!./modules/_a.js"], {
  import: "default",

});

title: proxy rewrite function to contain server
body:
### Description

as a dev testing my FE with multiple backend envs, i want to be able to have conditional rewrite based on server domain.

### Suggested solution

maybe a few possibilities
1. add a 2nd param to the `rewrite` fn which is equal to the `target`
2. change `path: string` to be `url: URL` with url.hostname matching `target`. instead of `rewrite` this could be seen as `beforeReroute` hook, sort of

### Alternative

what we do so far is:

```js
const BACKEND_URL = process.env.BACKEND_URL ?? 'https://our-staging-env'
```

then

```js
proxy: {
  '/api': {
    target: BACKEND_URL,
      changeOrigin: true,
        rewrite: (path) => {
          const hasOldUrlScheme = ['https://some-old-env-v1'].includes(BACKEND_URL)
          return !hasOldUrlScheme ? path.replace(some-rule) : path
        },
    },
}
```

but we need to define the BACKEND_URL outside of the vite config and reuse it in 2 separate (potentially unsynced) places

### Additional context

i'm well aware this is an edge case only for the convenience of a few and that the alternative provided is good enough as it is even tho it feels playing against the tool.

title: [docs] Default production target is confusing
body:
### Documentation is

- [ ] Missing
- [X] Outdated
- [X] Confusing
- [ ] Not sure?

### Explain in Detail

Hi!
Default [browser compatibility for production](https://vitejs.dev/guide/build.html#browser-compatibility) seems to be outdated or confusing.

The text says that it's "support for es modules, dynamic import and import.meta", however chrome version seems to be too high (so are others, chrome is just an example). According to caniuse, minimal chrome version that supports all of this features is chrome 64 ([^1], [^2], [^3]).

I believe the confusion comes from https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/2976. And chrome 87 was chosen arbitrary as it was what browserslist said at the time.

Today [the query](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/2976#issuecomment-831253198) returns quite a different result ([playground](https://browsersl.ist/#q=defaults+and+supports+es6-module+and+supports+es6-module-dynamic-import%2C+not+opera+%3E+0%2C+not+samsung+%3E+0%2C+not+and_qq+%3E+0)). Note that I'm not including the `import.meta` since there's no query for that but it shouldn't matter.

So, as a result the docs (and default target) are stuck in a weird place. It's not the _minimal viable_ version neither it is a _current recommended_ version. It's somewhere arbitrary in the middle.

[^1]: https://caniuse.com/es6-module
[^2]: https://caniuse.com/es6-module-dynamic-import
[^3]: https://caniuse.com/mdn-javascript_operators_import_meta

### Your Suggestion for Changes

I think the docs should mention both minimal and recommended versions in terms of browserslist queries.

Minimal version is almost the same as the `supports es6-module and supports es6-module-dynamic-import`, minus a couple of browser versions for `import.meta`.

Recommended one is kinda weird though, since `defaults` now almost fully covers everything that vite relies on ([playground for browsers that are in defaults, but don't have es modules or dynamic import](https://browsersl.ist/#q=defaults+and+not+supports+es6-module+and+not+supports+es6-module-dynamic-import))

Another question is what to do with default build target. We can leave it the same, since we don't want to break stuff. Or we can bump it to another arbitrary value, but it would get outdated right away. Imo the solution is to resolve `defaults` to esbuild targets, but it's outside of the scope of this issue.

title: Expose AST of import statement to resolveId hooks
body:
### Description

The `vite-tsconfig-paths` plugin currently does not rewrite imports, which [could be useful](https://github.com/aleclarson/vite-tsconfig-paths/issues/117) when combined with `vite-plugin-dts`. If I was to add that feature to `vite-tsconfig-paths`, I think the best way would be for Vite to give me the AST information it already has, which I could combine with `magic-string` to rewrite the aliased imports into relative imports. This would ensure that import statements emitted in `.d.ts` files would work outside the library's local setup.

### Suggested solution

At the very least, expose the location (start and end offsets) of the import specifier node through the `resolveId` options object.

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/5ee6fd2e830cce04e7bc8f0e9d7d69d7acb3eb2b/packages/vite/src/node/plugin.ts#L148-L157

That would be enough information to *easily and efficiently* implement import rewriting from a plugin's `transform` hook. So the plugin would cache the node locations it gets from `resolveId` and use them in its `transform` hook.

Note: This solution would likely require changes to Rollup as well.

title: Minification issue when using `image-set(…)`

A CSS rule like the following will cause a minification issue during builds using the default (PostCSS) pipeline:

```css
body {
  background-image: image-set("./assets/image1.avif" 1x,"./assets/image2.avif" 2x);

}

title: preload of explicit URL imports
body:
### Description

Currently there is no reasonable way to use explicit URL imports with [resource preloading](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preload), especially resources which specifires requires to be resolved with node resolution algorithm

### Suggested solution

introduce additional specifier suffix, resulting in resolved url being included in input html as preload link

as draft i propose `?url&preload=<type of resource>&crossorigin=<crossorigin mode>`

### Alternative

include preload link into input html file with manually resolved path

### Additional context

example:

let's introduce `wasm` package which exports `.wasm` file alongside with `.js` file
```
{
    "name": "wasm",
    "exports": {
        ".": "./src/index.js",
        "./mod.wasm": "./src/mod.wasm"
    }
}
```
then in application code we can import wasm file url with bare specifiers to fetch it, but we can not easily add corresponding preload link
```
import url from "wasm/mod.wasm?url";
```
preload link can be added only with full path
```
<link rel="preload" as="fetch" crossorigin="anonymous" href="node_modules/wasm/src/mod.wasm" />
```
and only this way its getting transformed into proper preload link after build
```
<link rel="preload" as="fetch" crossorigin="anonymous" href="/assets/mod-Cr-pdXkF.wasm" />
```

### Describe the ~~bug~~ feature (it's a feature I guess)

Context: Resolving external deps in `vite.config.ts`

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/128f09eb0100e80f566e33ca8c55bcd0896d4e38/packages/vite/src/node/config.ts#L983-L984

`conditions` is always empty, but we can specify a value via `node --conditions=dev` or `NODE_OPTIONS='--conditions=dev' node`.


## Suggested solution

I suggest that we should read both `process.env` and `process.execArgv`, and parse & merge them. It's a bit complex because there are tons of options in Node (and V8).

Or we can just use a Regex to match it.
```
// 3 cases
node --conditions=dev
node --conditions dev
node -C dev
```

Therefore, I wonder if there is a better solution can this issue.

title: import.meta.glob from node_modules caches project files incorrectly
body:
### Describe the bug

If a library in `node_modules` uses `import.meta.glob`, any files loaded by the glob are loaded using the same caching policy as the library.

For example, in [git@github.com:SystemParadox/vite-cache-issue.git](https://github.com/SystemParadox/vite-cache-issue.git), the network tab of devtools shows that `mylib.js` and `foo.svelte` both use `?v=2061e277` and are both cached aggressively.

This means that if for example `foo.svelte` is loaded initially but then something causes a dependency reoptimisation reload, then the browser will use its cached version of `foo.svelte` which is incorrect.

Combined with https://github.com/sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte/issues/1032 this also results in svelte styles randomly disappearing in our application.






### Reproduction

title: Style injection conflicts with SSR hydration on document
body:
### Describe the bug

tl;dr: vite dev injected `<style>` tags maybe removed by preact's hydration on `<html>` element.

Actually my SSR framework renders the whole `<html>` tag and I was trying to figure out how to deal with the styles in dev server.

Suppose I have a project like this:

```tsx
// App.tsx
import "./app.css"; // any styles
export function App() {
  return <html>
    <head> ... </head>
    <body> ... </body>
  </html>
}
```

```tsx
// entry.tsx
import { render } from 'preact';
import { App } from './App.tsx';
render(<App />, document, document.documentElement);
```

And in server side, I just have something like this:

```js
import { render } from 'preact-render-to-string';
import { App } from './App.tsx';
// when request coming
const html = render(<App />); // <html><head>...</head><body>...</body></html>
return new Response('<!DOCTYPE html>' + html);
```

The code above could work for production build, as I can read the manifest file and know which entry requires which style and inject them into the final html code. However, when I was using dev server, I don't know how many styles there in the project, and I can only rely on vite's dynamic style injection. Here comes the problem.

To describe the problem more accurately, let's think it step by step after open browser:

1. client start import "./entry.tsx"
2. continue import "./App.tsx"
3. continue import "./app.css", the injection code `__vite__updateStyle` runs, a style tag injected to head
4. the hydrate function in "./entry.tsx" runs and everything just added got removed

After these steps, no styles can get rendered.

title: Automatic Updating of the main property of package.json
body:
### Description

When vite builds for production, it postfixes a random string to the end of the bundle.  

It would be nice if we could configure vite to automatically update the `main` field of package.json to point to bundle each time a build is run. It's possible to make the bundle name fixed, but that [has a few drawbacks](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79535425/are-there-any-drawbacks-to-changing-the-vite-production-bundle-name-to-a-static).

title: package.json "exports" with array matcher only takes first
body:
### Describe the bug

I have a monorepo package with a `package.json` file that uses an `"exports"` key like,

```json
{
  "exports": {
    "./*": [
      "./*.tsx",
      "./*.ts",
      "./*.d.ts",
      "./*"
    ]
  }
}
```

It appears that when I import a `.ts` file from this package from an external module, Vite fails to find it, giving me an error,

```
Failed to resolve import '...'. Does the file exist?
```

The filename is `useDebounce.ts`. I know for fact that the file exists, and can even be accessed by control-clicking in VSCode.

See below for the reason this occurs. I debugged the Vite runtime and traced in Vite's source where the actual issue occurs.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-nvvs15ct?file=packages%2Fmy-package%2Fpackage.json

### Steps to reproduce

See the StackBlitz example:

In this example, I put `.ts` first, but imported a `.tsx` file.

The error will occur when running `npm run dev` from the root directory (or from `/apps/main`).

To see that it works when the necessary extension is first in the array, simply swap `.ts` with `.tsx` in the array under `"exports"`.

### System Info

```shell
N/A
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

## Debugger Trace Report

When I debugged Vite's resolution process, I came to this point:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3f1e5a4-0ab3-4bdf-a33b-b51806b41919)

Source position: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/dc5395a27e44066ef7725278c4057d9f1071a53f/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L1020

You can see `useDebounce.ts` is in the list returned from the `resolve.exports` module at index 1, but it appears that `resolveExportsOrImports` blindly takes only the first result, which is `useDebounce.tsx`, which does not exists.

It does appear that there's a spot in [tryCleanFsResolve](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/dc5395a27e44066ef7725278c4057d9f1071a53f/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L628) that attempts to resolve the file with various extensions (including .ts) but it passes the [tryResolveRealFileWithExtensions](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/dc5395a27e44066ef7725278c4057d9f1071a53f/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L1221) function a file with an extension already, in my case useDebounce.tsx. So it tries resolving files like useDebounce.tsx.ts / useDebounce.tsx.json / etc. If this was supposed to catch this case, then this is where the bug actually is.

Otherwise, the issue is that `resolve.exports` responds with a multi-element array, but `resolveExportsOrImports` only regards the first element.

(A temporary work-around is to make sure `./*.tsx` first and use the `.tsx` extension for all files, but this may be impractical for some projects.)

title: Confusing `buildStart` behavior with `createServer` API
body:
### Describe the bug

- Related https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/7479

Vite-node has been using a following style of programmatic server setup https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/94b27af595b5029b6201a7bcf2702169fe7ae6a4/packages/vite-node/src/cli.ts#L86-L99, but I'm not sure whether `buildStart` should be manually triggered on Vite 6 (also how `perEnvironmentStartEndDuringDev` should be enabled on server level or plugin level).

```js
const server = await createServer({});
await server.pluginContainer.buildStart({})
```

One issue with manually calling `buildStart` is that:

```js
// repro1.js
const server = await createServer({
    configFile: false,
    plugins: [
      {
        name: 'repro',
        async buildStart() {
          console.log('[repro:buildStart:in]');
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500));
          console.log('[repro:buildStart:out]');
        },
        transform(_code, id) {
          console.log('[repro:transform]', id);
        },
      },
    ]
});
await server.pluginContainer.buildStart({})
await server.ssrLoadModule("./src/empty.js");
```

which causes `transform` to happen before `buildStart` finishes:

```sh
$ node repro1.js 
[repro:buildStart:in]
[repro:transform] /xxx/src/empty.js
[repro:buildStart:out]
```

Probably this was the cause of https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/7479 and this can potentially break `vite:client-inject` since its `transform` relies on `buildStart`

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/7e7b6608f997fe8e69c891f064edcb7a62740373/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/clientInjections.ts#L102

On the other hand, one issue with not manually calling `buildStart` is that this breaks css import like in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/19606.

```js
// repro2.js
  const server = await createServer({
    configFile: false,
  });
  await server.ssrLoadModule("./src/import-css.js");
```

```sh
$ node repro2.js 
12:16:38 PM [vite] (ssr) Error when evaluating SSR module ./src/import-css.js: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')
  Plugin: vite:css-post
  File: /home/hiroshi/code/personal/reproductions/vite-19598-ssr-only-css/src/style.css

title: Give us a config to prevent the entire page load and only load the changed file in HMR
body:
### Description

Sometimes when I change a file in VS Code, I see these lines:

Container  | 2025-02-28T17:05:05.955Z vite:hmr [file change] src/Contents/Admin/Menu.jsx
Container  | 5:05:05 PM [vite] (client) page reload src/Contents/Admin/Menu.jsx

I once opened https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/15479, thus I learned one or two things about HMR.

But there is a problem here. My codebase has more than 2000 files. Reloading the page takes 50 seconds. Is it possible to somehow configure Vite and `react-refresh` to just send the currently changed file to the browser?

This is my `Menu.jsx`:

```
import AbcIcon from "@mui/icons-material/Abc"

const ContentsMenu = [
    {
        title: "ContentsContents",
        icon: AbcIcon,
        path: "/contents/parts"
    }
]

export default ContentsMenu
```

It's valid JS. Though it's not a React component, it's valid JS. Each part/module exposes its menu, and then the main `Menu.jsx` which is a valid React component collects those `Menu.jsx` files:

```
import { ContactsMenu } from "Contacts"

const Menu = [
    ...ContactsMenu
]
```

Then the `Menu.jsx` which is a React component imports the main `Menu.jsx` and renders it.

So:

1. Each part/module has a `Menu.jsx` file in which it describes its menu as a simple JS array
2. The main `Menu.jsx` in the application imports and merges `Menu.jsx` from parts/modules and exports them as a simple JS array
3. The `Menu.jsx` component in the admin panel imports the aggregates menu and renders it

This architecture is extremely useful for us. It's valid JS and we have had this architecture for over a decade now (in jQuery, then in Angular.js, then in Angular, then in React).

But whenever we save any of those `Menu.jsx` files that export a JS array, we see a complete page reload which in our huge project causes more than 50 seconds of wait. This extremely degrades the DX.


### Suggested solution

I don't know about the complexities and internals of HMR, but I think letting a simple JS file be loaded without a page reload would be possible. Because it's a simple chain of usage. And we can configure it. For example:

```
{
    hmr: {
        loadIndividually: ["Menu.jsx"]
    }
}
```

### Alternative

No alternative. Right now we're suffering. That's all. We fear changing `Menu.jsx` files. Sometimes we close the browser, change some files together, and then reopen the browser and enter the address to prevent multiple consecutive reloads.

title: Vite 6 does not load `/assets/img/**` as Vite 5 does
body: ### Describe the bug Hello, I'm currently facing two issues while updating to Vite 6. **First one:** I made a plugin to dynamically load images from the `/assets/img` folder we can use `$img('image-path')` to reference any image inside `/assets/img` even if it is in a subfolder like `/img/subfolder/image.png`, this works fine in Vite 5 but does not in Vite 6. Please check attached [Reproduction Repo](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-pqa9sp4z?file=src%2Fplugins%2Fimg.js) and see video below to better understand. i'm using `new URL().href` to obtain image path and then reference it, in my `$img()` plugin we can pass any image path and the function will return the URL to use in `` tags, this is working fine in Vite 5. Just by updating to Vie 6 the function stops working, I read the [upgrade guide](https://vite.dev/guide/migration.html) and research on simimilar issues but any of them solved this problem. **My research** Notice that `img1.svg` is on `/assets/img` and `img2.svg` is on a subfolder of `/assets/img`, I believe the issue comes from the side of Vite 6not being able to deep iterate inside `/assets/img` to see nested folders and images as Vite 5 did, Looks like in Vite 5 all images under `/assets/` were moved to the final app build, but looks like this is no longer the case in Vite 6. I didn't find any configuration to revert that behavior, looks like it is an internal change that generated a breaking change. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69ac5707-bedd-4fc3-89f7-c72c5df927f6 **Second Issue:** This statement works different on Vite 5 than in Vite 6 during Development and Build. One change i found that could be related is this PR #18194 Vite 5: Works fine in both Dev and Prod ```js new URL(`../assets/img/${imgPath}`).href // Returns: `http://localhost/src/assets/img/{imgPath}` // Works fine and returns correct URL to use on Production ``` Vite 6: ```js new URL(`../assets/img/${imgPath}`).href // Returns: `http://localhost/src/assets/undefined` // Does not work with interpolation as used to in Vite 5 // if we switch to "string" + variable it works again but not in production ``` ### Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-pqa9sp4z?file=src%2FApp.vue ### Steps to reproduce 1. `npm i && npm run dev` with vite 5, check images are correct. 2. `npm run build && npm run preview` check images still visible using the function. 3. title: about '\0' prefix, resolvId() retrun the prefixed virtual modules Id, but it isn't prefixed in load() hook.
body:
### Describe the bug

env: vite 6.2.0

About the '\0' prefix. [Link](https://vite.dev/guide/api-plugin.html#virtual-modules-convention. ) 

Office example: 
``` js
export default function myPlugin() {
  const virtualModuleId = 'virtual:my-module'
  const resolvedVirtualModuleId = '\0' + virtualModuleId

  return {
    name: 'my-plugin', // required, will show up in warnings and errors
    resolveId(id) {
      if (id === virtualModuleId) {
        return resolvedVirtualModuleId
      }
    },
    load(id) {
      if (id === resolvedVirtualModuleId) {  // This Line, id isn't has '\0' prefix
        return `export const msg = "from virtual module"`
      }
    },
  }
}
```

But in my plugin, I found that the behavior is inconsistent with the examples on the '\0' prefix.

Office example: The prefixed virtual module id is returned in `resolveId` hook. And then, **the prefixed virtual module id** is used in the `load` hook (  `if (id === resolvedVirtualModuleId) {  ......` ). 
example: id: `'virtual:my-module'`, resolved return: `'\0virtual:my-module'`, in load hook id param: `'\0virtual:my-module'`.

In my plugin development, I found that I return the '\0' prefixed virtual module id in resolveId hook, 
but  it isn't prefixed in load hook. 
example: id: `'virtual:my-module'`, resolved return: `'\0virtual:my-module'`, in load hook id param: `'virtual:my-module'`.

In addition, in configureServer hook, the prefix is the same as in the official website example `/@id/__x00__{id}`

I suspect that the official website example is misleading, or there may be  other reasons.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-1z2fxnqj?file=vite.config.js

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run 'npm install' and 'npm run dev'.
2. Wait for browser loaded, the `Terminal` will print result.

`resolveId` return `'\0'` prefixed id, `load` will print non-prefiexed virtual module id, opposite to office example.

### Describe the bug

title: Better Support for Debugging Config
body:
### Description

As a developer using Vite I want to be able to debug my code in `vite.config.ts` via VSCode  so I can troubleshoot any problems in plugins or other code snippets added in the file.

I start the debugging by adding `debugger;` statements and then launch vite via: 

* using vite commands in the JavaScript Debug Terminal
* Opening the package.json and hit debug on the inline hint 


### Suggested solution

Vite currently deletes the temporary `node_modules/.vite-temp/vite.config.ts.timestamp-....` file after it was loaded:

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c9e086d35ac35ee1c6d85d48369e8a67a2ba6bfe/packages/vite/src/node/config.ts#L1999-L2012

It would be great if Vite would detect that a debugger is currently attached and keep the file in this case. 

According to [this StackOverflow Post](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67445850) this could be achieved by checking whether there is a inspector url defined (works fine for me in VSCode). But also to check for some [special node argvs](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/9617#issuecomment-326075501) is a potential candidate. 

My proposal would be to use something like: 
```js
import inspector from 'inspector';

function isInDebugMode() {
    const argv = process.execArgv.join();
    return inspector.url() !== undefined || argv.includes('inspect') || argv.includes('debug') || process.env.VITE_KEEP_CONFIG;
}
```

### Alternative

1. Only add an environment variable. (a bit less convienient as you have to remember to set it every time).
2. Add a config key which can be filled by the user to keep the transpiled config.
3. Ensure (somehow?) that sourcemaps are working and breakpoints can be set in the original file directly. Currently source maps are generated but they do not work for VS Code Debugging.  

### Additional context

https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/9617
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c9e086d35ac35ee1c6d85d48369e8a67a2ba6bfe/packages/vite/src/node/config.ts#L1999-L2012

title: Documentation of `build-manifest` is Confusing
body: ### Documentation is - [ ] Missing - [ ] Outdated - [x] Confusing - [ ] Not sure? ### Explain in Detail On the [build-manifest](https://vite.dev/config/build-options.html#build-manifest) part deal with the manifest.json file. When this option is set to true, the build process generates a manifest file at the default location `(.vite/manifest.json)`, which contains a mapping of unhashed asset filenames to their hashed versions for use by server frameworks. However, when the option is set to a string, that string is not only used as the manifest file name but also changes the entire output file path. In this case, the default `.vite` directory and its contents will not be generated; instead, the files are output to a new path defined by the provided string. This behavior may confuse users who expect only the manifest file name to change. ### Your Suggestion for Changes I suggest updating the documentation as follows: ``` When set to true, the build will also generate a .vite/manifest.json file that contains a mapping of non-hashed asset filenames to their hashed versions, which can then be used by a server framework to render the correct asset links. When the value is a string, it will be used as the manifest file name. ::: tip Note: When this option is set to a string, that string will be used as the manifest file name, and the default .vite directory along with its contents will not be generated. Instead, the files will be output to a new path as defined by the string. ::: ``` This clarification will help ensure users fully understand the impact of using a string value for this configuration option. ### Reproduction _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce ## set `manifest` of `true` ## set `manifest` of `manifest.json`

body:
### Describe the bug

In vite ssr, if I separate vite config logic to different files like `vite.client.config.ts` and `vite.server.config.ts`, and I get `viteDevServer` instance by calling `createServer` method use these configurations.

On the server side, I use `ssrLoadModule` in the viteDevServer instance, like

```js
const viteServer = await createServer(serverConfig)
await (viteServer as ViteDevServer).ssrLoadModule(viteServerEntry)
```

On the client side, I use a ViteDevServer instance with middleware mode, like

```js
const viteServer: ViteDevServer = await createServer(clientConfig)
proxyMiddlewaresArr.push(viteServer.middlewares)
```

It's a common practice in server-side render projects. But in `rolldown-vite`, the websocket server will call the listen function twice because `createServer` is called twice. In my opinion, there is no need to create a Websocket server when I only use `ViteDevServer` for `ssrLoadModule`.

title: WebWorker URL is not properly resolved in dev pre-bundled dependency
body:
### Describe the bug

I'm trying to use the `@aztec/bb.js` library that has an asynchronous function that loads a web worker, using the regular syntax:
```js
const worker = new Worker(new URL('./main.worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' });
```

Unfortunately, it seems vite pre-bundling breaks when this function is actually called, as the URL ends up being rewritten as `node_modules/.vite/deps/main.worker.js?worker_file&type=module`, which doesn't actually exist (it does get rewritten, as you can see, so that's not the issue itself, but the path is incorrect).

I do get the helpful error below, which ends up working (see commented out code in repro-directory vite.config.ts).
```
The file does not exist at "node_modules/.vite/deps/main.worker.js?worker_file&type=module" which is in the optimize deps directory. The dependency might be incompatible with the dep optimizer. Try adding it to `optimizeDeps.exclude`.
```
If I exclude the dependency, things work out as the relative paths are preserved.

Opening the issue because this seems like a somewhat common problem potentially, and I'm not 100% sure where it goes wrong - maybe vite just confuses the path of the prebundled dependency with the path of the original query, in which case maybe the worker URL should be rewritten when pre-bundling? Maybe some other thing.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/hyli-org/vite-bb-worker-issue

### Steps to reproduce

Run `npm install` then `rpm run dev`. On loading the server, you should get an URL that fails to load, the above described warning, and note that indeed this file does not exist.

title: CSS Modules 场景下 :global 里的 keyframes 失效
Support --force (and/or pass-through of Vite flags) in vike CLI
body:
### Description

## Context
Vike CLI currently supports only the options `--host`, `--port`, and `--mode`.  
Other Vite CLI flags such as `--force` aren’t available. This makes cache-busting flows awkward compared to using the Vite CLI directly.

Reference: [Vike CLI docs](https://vike.dev/cli) – only the three options above are listed as supported.

## Expected
Running:
```bash
vike dev --force
vike build --force
````

should behave like Vite (ignoring prebundled cache and forcing a fresh build).

## Actual

`vike` ignores `--force`; only the three aliased flags are recognized.

## Why it matters

* Developer ergonomics: quickly fixing stale prebundle/cache issues without custom scripts.
* Parity with Vite CLI expectations (`--force` is common in Vite workflows).
* Keeps one entry point (`vike`) instead of swapping back to `vite` just to use CLI flags.

## Workarounds

* Manually remove the cache folder:

  ```bash
  rm -rf node_modules/.vite && vike dev
  ```
* Configure `cacheDir` in `vite.config.ts` or add a pre-script that wipes `.vite`.



## Proposal

* Add `--force` as a supported Vike setting, similar to `--host`, `--port`, and `--mode`.
* (Optional) Provide a generic pass-through mechanism for other Vite flags, so users don’t hit this again for flags like `--clearScreen`.

title: Respect Browserslist config in esbuild
body:
### Description

esbuild doesn’t have built-in Browserslist config.

Benefits:
* Autoprefixer, postcss-preset-env, Babel and many other tools have. So users may expect Browserslist config.
* It is great to have only single config to specify target browsers for all tools.
* With Browserslist config, we can reduce polyfills in esbuild output and make JS works faster.

### Suggested solution

We can use [`browserslist-to-esbuild`](https://github.com/marcofugaro/browserslist-to-esbuild) as suggested in [When Vite ignores your Browserslist configuration](https://dev.to/meduzen/when-vite-ignores-your-browserslist-configuration-3hoe) article.

In this case, Vite will look for Browserslist config and auto-fill [`build.target`](https://vitejs.dev/config/build-options.html#build-target) config option.

### Alternative

_No response_

### Additional context

Browserslist also supports Node.js versions

title: The ability to predefine scaffolding parameters from the command line for `create-vite` and ask for the rest interactively
body:
### Description

I'm working on a template for applications. The template is built as a mono-repository, in which the UI is an independent package based on vite. 

In such a structure, the UI can be any option provided by `create-vite` tool, but there are still parts that needs to be properly setup.

For example, regardless of the UI stack, its package name must be specific so that other packages in the mono repository can refer to it. 

### Suggested solution

It would be useful to be able to predefine some parameters on the command line, such as the package name, and ask the user interactively during deployment.

```
npm create vite -- --set.packageName=@myrepo/name
```
This command will start interactive mode and ask user about framework and TS etc and skip prompt for package name.

title: styles is not removed when css import is removed from non hmr module
body:
### Describe the bug

- Related https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/20768

For HMR, Vite removes styles using prune event, but this is currently triggered only when an import is removed from a module which has `import.meta.hot`.

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/bb29b04e88ba1befa4a66e265809b0216cdbcddb/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/importAnalysis.ts#L458-L462

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/84079a84ad94de4c1ef4f1bdb2ab448ff2c01196/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/importAnalysis.ts#L829-L840

This can causes an issue where style removal doesn't happen when modifying non-self-accepting module, for example:

app.jsx : self accepting

title: `environments.ssr.build.emitAssets: true` not working when `builder.sharedConfigBuild: true`
body:
### Describe the bug

With a following config:

```js
export default defineConfig({
  environments: {
    client: {
      build: {
        outDir: 'dist/client',
        rollupOptions: {
          input: './src/client.ts',
        },
      },
    },
    ssr: {
      build: {
        outDir: 'dist/ssr',
        emitAssets: true,
        rollupOptions: {
          input: './src/ssr.ts',
        },
      },
    },
  },
  builder: {
    sharedPlugins: true,
    sharedConfigBuild: true,
    async buildApp(builder) {
      console.log(
        '[client/emitAssets]',
        builder.environments.client.config.build.emitAssets
      ); // ==> true
      await builder.build(builder.environments.client);
      console.log(
        '[ssr/emitAssets]',
        builder.environments.ssr.config.build.emitAssets
      ); // ==> false
      await builder.build(builder.environments.ssr);
    },
  },
});
```

SSR build doesn't generate assets.

```sh
$ vite build
[client/emitAssets] true

title: Pseudo element selectors with nested @starting-style doesn't build correctly
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi,

When you have a nested `@starting-style` inside a pseudo-element selector, it works in development but doesn't work after the build, the CSS build output is wrong.

Here is an example:
```css
dialog {
  margin: auto;
}

dialog::backdrop {
  background: #2E368C7F;
  transition: opacity 1s ease-in;

  @starting-style {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

Here is the CSS output (after build):
```css
dialog{margin:auto}dialog::backdrop{background:#2e368c7f;transition:opacity 1s ease-in}@starting-style{{opacity:0}}
```
Formated output:
```css
dialog {
  margin: auto
}

dialog::backdrop {
  background: #2e368c7f;
  transition: opacity 1s ease-in
}

@starting-style {
    {
    opacity: 0
  }
}
```

The `@starting-style` get's placed outside the original selector. If the objective is to place it outside, it needs to have the pseudo-element selector inside it.

Placing the `@starting-style` inside a selector isn't invalid syntax: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@starting-style#syntax

It doesn't have to be `::backdrop`, it happens with any pseudo-element selector (e.g. `::after`, `::before`) based on my tests.

Reproduction:
[vite-nested-starting-style-bug-demo](https://github.com/machadinhos/vite-nested-starting-style-bug-demo)

title: Expose more functions from `build`
body:
### Description

In our project, we use vite with some custom plugins. In one of these plugins, we need to bundle ourselves using rollup. Additionally, we need to pass the worker plugins to rollup. This works fine in vite 5. However, the changes to vite 6 (and also vite 7) introduces changes to how such plugins are applied in rollup. In particular, the following does not work anymore because the plugins are not properly applied:
```
// vite > 6
const bundle = await rollup.rollup({
   input: resolved.id, // pass in some custom `ResolvedId`
   plugins: plugins: config.worker.plugins // pass in the resolved config. In vite 5, we passed it with config.worker.plugins([]) which worked fine
```
We found in your source code in `worker.ts` that you apply the environment to the plugins using `injectEnvironmentToHooks`. Consequently, we made a custom build that exposes this function and got it to work.

Is there a specific reason that you don't expose this function? 
Is there a way to expose this function to the client?
And if not, is there a way to reproduce this behavior using the functions that vite exposes?

### Suggested solution

Please expose more functions to the client to work with the new `Environment API` or point us to how we can manually invoke rollup with vite plugins.

title: (Error) Vite in its latest version does not install the rollup module for android arm64
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi, I'm a small Front-end developer working from my Android phone since I don't have a PC or laptop. I've been doing my practice and projects from my phone, using React, Tailwind, HTML, and CSS for the time being. I use Termux as a terminal and to install and run my projects, etc. However, in this latest version of Vite, there's a problem running my React project (npm run dev). It says the Android Arm64 rollup module is needed, and Vite apparently didn't install it. This error didn't happen in previous versions, and I'd like to report this bug since some people don't have a PC to practice or run projects and have to use other alternatives.

In my case, I solved the error by pasting the code into Vite's package.json file to fix the rollup error.

This is the code I used to fix the installation error that Vite has on mobile devices, in my case, Android (which didn't happen in previous versions of Vite).

"overrides": {
"@rollup/rollup-android-arm64": "4.45.1"
}

Please, it would be a great help to fix this issue for future versions of Vite and better consider Android. Thanks for reading.

Please take more into account ARM, ARM64 and Android, because although it may not seem like it, people who use these alternatives do not necessarily do so for pleasure, but because not everyone can afford a laptop or PC to work or at least practice coding for personal reasons and have to require available alternatives. We appreciate that this issue be seen, taken into account and solved in future versions, thank you.

title: Setting `css.preprocessorOptions.scss.fatalDeprecations` using a `Version` causes `obsolete` deprecations to log warnings
body:
### Describe the bug

My goal is to automatically set the `fatalDeprecations` using the current version of `sass` from our `package.json`. That way when it gets bumped, we are forced to fix those deprecations.

If I set `fatalDeprecations` using `Version.parse`, then all of the deprecations that are also obsolete are also getting added. This seems to cause the sass compiler to spit out warnings like the following

```
Warning: mixed-decls deprecation is obsolete, so does not need to be made fatal.

Warning: type-function deprecation is obsolete, so does not need to be made fatal
```

Adding `mixed-decls` and `type-functions` to `silenceDeprecations` causes the following warnings

```
Warning: mixed-decls deprecation is obsolete. If you were previously silencing it, your code may now behave in unexpected ways.

Warning: type-function deprecation is obsolete. If you were previously silencing it, your code may now behave in unexpected ways.
```

Ideally, `Version.parse` would not include any deprecations that are obsolete, so we can always use the latest version and be up-to-date on our deprecations.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-daxkrf7y?file=src%2Fmain.js

### Steps to reproduce

1) Add `sass` as a dependency
1) Set `css.preprocessorOptions.scss.fatalDeprecations` to `Version.parse("1.92.1")`
1) Make a `.scss` file and use it
1) Run either `vite build` or `vite` and see warnings

title: Terser nameCache is broken by multi-threaded mode, causing object key–value mismatches in different chunks
body: ### Describe the bug When nameCache is provided, it gets cloned for each worker thread, resulting in isolated caches that are not synchronized back to the main thread. This inconsistency can cause key–value mismatches for the same type of object in different chunks, making the `nameCache` ineffective and leading to incorrect minification results. ### Reproduction https://github.com/AntaresQAQ/vite-terser-bug-repro ### Steps to reproduce ### Vite Config ```ts import { defineConfig } from "vite"; const nameCache = {}; // https://vite.dev/config/ export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ { name: "terser-mangle-props-cache", closeBundle() { console.log("Name cache:", nameCache); }, }, ], build: { minify: "terser", terserOptions: { compress: false, mangle: { properties: true, }, nameCache, }, }, }); ``` ### Codes `obj1.ts` ```ts import type { IDemoObj } from "./types"; const obj: IDemoObj = { baz: "baz", foo: "foo", qux: "qux", bar: "bar", }; export default obj; ``` `src/obj2.ts` ```ts import type { IDemoObj } from "./types"; const obj: IDemoObj = { foo: "foo", bar: "bar", baz: "baz", qux: "qux", }; export default obj; ``` ### Built files 1. chunk `obj1-Ds7_RE47.js` ```js const a={o:"baz",t:"foo",u:"qux",q:"bar"};export{a as default}; title: .json files are imported as an object even with `?no-inline`
body:
### Describe the bug

`import asset from './example.json?no-inline` is not enough to get a string URL of the asset location. Instead, it imports the asset as an object.

Meanwhile, `import asset from './example.json?url'` imports the asset as a base64 string if it's small enough to be inlined.

Alternatively, combining `url` and `no-inline` provides the URL string but the type definition doesn't exist.
```js
import asset from './example.json?url&no-inline'; // type error
```

Should we simply add the type definition for `?url&no-inline` or should importing with `?no-inline` be enough to get the string URL?

title: Share chunks between multiple ESM Workers
body:
### Describe the bug

When bundling WebWorkers in the `es` format, all the modules imported by the worker are inlined inside the worker chunk and no import syntax is used.

In the following reproduction, there's the following setup:

* 2 script outputs: `main` and `seconday`
* One module `validation` that is imported by `main.ts` and `secondary.ts`

By analyzing the build output, 3 chunks are emitted:
- `validation-[hash].js`, which includes the code shared between both `main` and `secondary` outputs.
- `main-[hash].js`, the code for the `main` output.
- `secondary-[hash].js`, the code for the `secondary` output.

For WebWorkers in ESM format, the same behaviour is expected: instead of inlining the imported modules in the worker's chunk, the worker should import from another common chunk.

Specifically, in the reproduction, I expect the shared chunk to contain the contents of ``isBool`` (from ``validation.ts``) and comlink's ``expose`` and that both are imported by the workers (``FancyWorker1`` just needs to import ``expose``).

To better see the problem, minification is already disabled.

related: #16719

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vue3-vite-typescript-starter-rayp8m

1. Run ``npm ci && npm run build`` in the StackBlitz project

title: Running `vite dev` doesn't exit with an error when there is a problem in the dependency optimisation step (esbuild)
body:
### Describe the bug

Currently in the Ember project we are using the command `vite optimize` to verify that all the dependencies are being optimised correctly (see [this test file](https://github.com/embroider-build/embroider/blob/main/tests/scenarios/vite-dep-optimizer-test.ts) if you're curious). With the recent deprecation of the `vite optimize` command https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/19348 we need a way to be able to verify the dependency optimisation step passes without error in our CI.

We can't rely on `vite dev` for this information because an esbuild plugin fails for any reason that dependency just gets externalised and will be re-loaded once the Vite dev server starts. You can see that behaviour in the linked reproduction.

Even if we don't make vite dev always fail for people if esbuild fails (maybe this is a default that might need to wait for a major?) we would love the ability to pass an arg that would opt-in to this behaviour e.g. `vite dev --brittle` or something

title: Performance issue: `vite dev` faster after running `vite build` once
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi,

I figured out that my `vite dev` starts faster if I do a `vite build` before.

It does not make any sense to me, so I did some research.

title: Rollup-Incompatible getModuleInfo behavior
body:
### Describe the bug

This tiny plugin always succeeds in rollup (and `vite build`) and always fails in `vite dev`:

```js
{
  name: 'example",
  load(id) {
    if (!this.getModuleInfo(id)) {
      throw new Error(`load should always see module info`);
    }
  },
}
```

Rollup promises to construct moduleInfo synchronously when any `load` is first started, and even shows an example of calling `this.load({ id })` *and not awaiting the promise* as a way to force `this.getModuleInfo(id).meta` to exist.

I think this disconnect is at the root of issues like https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/6766. 

From some [commentary](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7477#discussion_r860395660) on a related PR it sounds like it's a goal for Vite's module graph to not contain modules that haven't finished loading yet, but if that is true `getModuleInfo` needs to be driven at least partly from a different source of truth that *does* have entries for not-yet-loaded modules.

### Reproduction

title: Vite SSR doesn't overwrite `*` re-export by named export
body:
### Describe the bug

Example code

- dep.js

```js
export const a = "dep-a"
export const b = "dep-b"
export const c = "dep-c"
```

- main.js

```js
export const a = "main-a"
export * from "./dep.js"
export const c = "main-c"
```

#### expected

```sh
❯ node -e 'import("./src/main.js").then(console.log)'
[Module: null prototype] { a: 'main-a', c: 'main-c', b: 'dep-b' }
```

(Also rollup output on [repl](https://rollupjs.org/repl/?version=4.34.8&))

#### actual

```sh
# get "dep-a" instead of "main-a"
❯ node repro.js
{"a":"dep-a","b":"dep-b","c":"main-c"}
```

Side note: Current Vite SSR works if `export const` comes after `export *`. But, probably export hoisting PR https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/18983 currently breaks this pattern all the time. I think technically this is solvable if we gather local named export names first and then pass and exclude them from `exportAll` runtime function:

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c0e3dba3108e479ab839205cfb046db327bdaf43/packages/vite/src/module-runner/runner.ts#L407

title: tree-shaking/misleading warning "module has been externalized for browser compatibility"
body:
### Describe the bug

Vite emits a build warning if a node API is imported even though the code is never bundled for the client. 

Blocks [this issue](https://github.com/opral/inlang-paraglide-js/issues/403) in Paraglide JS. https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/5676 is likely related. 


### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-4ugmukbe?file=src%2Fmain.js

### Steps to reproduce

Run `npm install && npm run build`. 

The serverMiddleware code is never imported in the client-side code. Yet, Vite emits the build warning. 

```ts
async function serverMiddleware() {
  const { AsyncLocalStorage } = await import('async_hooks');
  console.log(AsyncLocalStorage);
}
```

title: Order of glob imported modules should be alphabetical
body:
### Documentation is

- [ ] Missing
- [ ] Outdated
- [x] Confusing
- [ ] Not sure?

### Explain in Detail

In [Features#Glob Import](https://vite.dev/guide/features#glob-import) all examples in generated code show something like:
```js
import * as __glob_0_0__ from "./foo.js"
import * as __glob_0_1__ from "./bar.js"
```
and in every example `foo` is before `bar`, but in reality glob and dir APIs return in almost alphabetical order: `bar` then `foo`.

### Your Suggestion for Changes

Show `bar` before `foo` in generated example results.

### Reproduction

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

title: Yarn, VSCode, react-ts, cannot find modules on new project
body:
### Describe the bug

I have run `yarn create vite my-app --template react-ts` and it has generated a project.

The project is not happy at all in VsCode and can not find any of the imported modules.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/748512e2-07c2-4923-b184-8b10ea9a4eb7)

For whatever reason the **reproduction URL does not suffer the same issue** and honestly, the issue seems to be with yarn using pnp.

I managed to make it work after generating the project and adding a .yarnrc.yml with 

```
enableGlobalCache: false
nodeLinker: node-modules
```


### Reproduction (Does not reproduce with the same steps as above)

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-d5pkqyku?file=react-ts%2Fsrc%2FApp.tsx

title: Vite module runner stacktrace on first line is incorrect
body:
### Describe the bug

Yet another very minor stack trace issue. It's likely due to `"use strict"` appended on runtime side evaluation. Recording it here so I have a place to point to for one test failure on oxc module runner https://github.com/vitejs/rolldown-vite/pull/85.

- repro3.js

```js
throw new Error('__TEST__')
```

- vite2.js

```js
import { createServerModuleRunner } from "vite";
import { createServer } from "vite";

async function main() {
  const server = await createServer({ configFile: false})
  const runner = createServerModuleRunner(server.environments.ssr, {
    // same issues for any interceptor
    sourcemapInterceptor: "prepareStackTrace"
  });
  await runner.import(process.argv[2]);
}

main()
```

On Node:

```js
$ node repro3.js
file:///dir/repro3.js:1
throw new Error('__TEST__')
      ^

Error: __TEST__
    at file:///dir/repro3.js:1:7
```

On Vite:

```js
$ node vite2.js repro3.js
[vite] connected.
/dir/repro3.js:3  <-- ❓ (probably rewriting this is not supported or node's bug)
"use strict";throw new Error('__TEST__')
                   ^

Error: __TEST__
    at /dir/repro3.js:1:18  <-- ❓❓
```

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/github/hi-ogawa/reproductions/tree/main/oxc-source-map-call-stack-column?file=README.md

Download stackblitz and test it locally

#### 6.1.x
```js
const outputFilePath = path.join(PATHS.source, outputFile);
const outputData = await import(outputFilePath, { assert: { type: 'json' } });
```

#### 6.0.1

const outputData = await import(outputFilePath, { with: { type: 'json' } });
```

```sh
node:internal/modules/esm/assert:88
        throw new ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING(url, 'type', validType);
              ^

TypeError [ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING]: Module "file:///Users/johnny/path/to/my/data.json" needs an import attribute of "type: json"

error Command failed

title: Transitive dependencies of linked dependencies are bundled in SSR build
body:
### Describe the bug

I have a pnpm monorepo containing packages `app` and `shared`. `app` depends on `shared`.

My expectation is that
- Vite will bundle `shared` in `app`'s SSR build for HMR, because it is a linked dependency and therefore is not externalized.
- `shared`'s dependencies in `shared/node_modules` remain external.

What actually happens is that Vite bundles `shared`'s dependencies into `app`'s SSR build as well as `shared` itself. This breaks our app because `shared` pulls in a CJS module (`require-in-the-middle`) which explodes if it is loaded in an ESM context (https://github.com/nodejs/require-in-the-middle/issues/110).

### Reproduction

https://github.com/haines/vite-ssr-externals-repro

### Steps to reproduce

Clone the repo and run `pnpm run repro` (which is equivalent to running `pnpm install` followed by `pnpm run build` and `pnpm run preview` in the `app`).

The SSR bundle `packages/app/dist/server/entry-server.js` will include `require-in-the-middle` rather than importing it from `packages/shared/node_modules`. This will cause the server to blow up with 

```
ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope, you can use import instead
This file is being treated as an ES module because it has a '.js' file extension and 'vite-ssr-externals-repro/packages/app/package.json' contains "type": "module". To treat it as a CommonJS script, rename it to use the '.cjs' file extension.
```

title: Dependencies added during a CSS transform opt-out of HMR
body:
### Describe the bug

When using `addWatchFile(…)` inside a `transform` hook on CSS files, the watched files will successfully trigger a rebuild of the CSS file whenever they change.

However, a rebuild triggered from the watched files will always cause a hard-refresh instead of a HMR refresh of the Stylesheet that happens when the CSS file changes on it's own.

This can be reproduced by a plugin like this:

```ts
function plugin(): Plugin {
  return {
    name: "my-plugin",
    async transform(content: string | undefined, id: string) {
      if (id.endsWith("main.css")) {
        this.addWatchFile(
          fileURLToPath(new URL("./articles/test.txt", import.meta.url))
        );
        return `/* ${Math.random()} */\n${content}`;
      }
    },
  };
}
```

In Tailwind CSS, we use `addWatchFile(…)` extensively to avoid setting up our own watchers. 


### Reproduction

https://github.com/philipp-spiess/vite-css-dependency-hard-refresh

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
pnpm build
pnpm vite dev
touch src/index.css # This triggers a HMR
touch artilces/test.txt # This triggers a hard-refresh
```

title: Vite module runner call stack column is slightly different from Node
body:
### Describe the bug

This is very minor difference, so it's not likely this matters for any users, but putting here for the record.

- repro2.js

```js
import { repro2Dep } from "./repro2-dep.js"

repro2Dep();
```

- repro2-dep.js

```js
export function repro2Dep() {
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 2;
  console.trace("__TEST__");
}

^ at repro2.js:3:1

title: Svelte CSS treeshaking not working
body:
### Describe the bug

We want to use the svelte kit library (building based on vite) configuration to build a component library that we integrate into a svelte kit app. When we import components as modules. For example like this:
```jsx
import { Heading } from "svelte-kit-library";
```
Then we get in the build files all css stylings of other components that are not used or imported in the application. If the components are imported explicitly, there are no unwanted stylings in the build files.
```jsx
import Heading from "svelte-kit-library/Heading.svelte";
```


### Reproduction

https://github.com/tomolenet/svelte-kit-treeshaking

### Steps to reproduce


In `packages/svelte-kit-app` we use the `packages/svelte-kit-library` in `src/routes/+page.svelte`. First use the module import in line 7.

```jsx
import { Heading } from "svelte-kit-library";
```

```bash
# build app
npm run build -w packages/svelte-kit-app

```

Now check the output `packages/svelte-kit-app/.svelte-kit`. If you search for `.unwanted` which is styling of the `Unwanted` component of `packages/svelte-kit-library` you realize that styling exists in the build result. However, we have not imported the component at any point in the project.  
Now change the import statement and use explicit import in line 10.

```jsx
import Heading from "svelte-kit-library/Heading.svelte";
```

```bash
# build app
npm run build -w packages/svelte-kit-app

```

Now the `.unwanted` class is no longer included in the build. It seems that the tree shaking does not work correctly at this point.

title: Option to prevent `link[rel="stylesheet"]` elements in index.html from being merged into a single `link[rel="stylesheet"]` element
body:
### Description

> As a developer using Vite
> I want multiple `link[rel="stylesheet"]` elements I put in index.html not being merged into a single `link[rel="stylesheet"]` element
> so that I can utilize each individual global stylesheet separately.

It seems that CSS WG is willing to lift the restriction on constructed flag for adoptedStylesheets: <https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/10013#issuecomment-2165396092>.
After the restriction is lifted, we can easily apply the stylesheet of one of the global `link[rel="stylesheet"]` to Shadow Roots.
(Even if the restriction is not lifted, we still have workarounds.)

<details open>
<summary>Example (vanilla + SCSS)</summary>

> https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-orv9nq?file=index.html
> `npm run dev` works as expected because CSS files are not merged during dev.
> `npm run build && npm run preview` doesn't work, because CSS files have been merged into a single file, and the element `link#bgRed` has gone.
</details>

Currently, since Vite always merge `link[rel="stylesheet"]` elements in index.html, we cannot do it this way.

### Suggested solution

Add an option, like:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    cssCodeSplitInIndexHtml: true
  },
});
```

to make `link[rel="stylesheet"]` elements in index.html not being merged.

### Alternative

- loading global styles using JavaScript, so that they can be separated: FOUC.
- putting global styles in index.html as well as loading them using JavaScript: duplication.

### Additional context

I opened a discussion some days ago: <https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/18632>.

title: Generate HTML Snippets for Backend Integration
body:
### Description

#### Background  
Vite provides the `build.manifest` option, which helps integrate with backend frameworks by describing the relationships between built JavaScript and CSS files. Backend frameworks typically parse `manifest.json` and generate `<script>` and `<link>` tags accordingly, embedding them into their templating systems.  

https://vite.dev/guide/backend-integration

Example `manifest.json`:
```json
{
  "views/foo.js": {
    "file": "assets/foo-BRBmoGS9.js",
    "name": "foo",
    "src": "views/foo.js",
    "isEntry": true,
    "imports": ["_shared-B7PI925R.js"],
    "css": ["assets/foo-5UjPuW-k.css"]
  }
}
```

#### Feature Proposal  
Instead of requiring backend frameworks to process `manifest.json` and generate HTML tags, Vite could provide an option to generate the necessary `<script>` and `<link>` tags directly. This would simplify integration with server-side frameworks, reducing the need for custom parsers or code generators on the backend side.  

According to Conway’s Law, system design tends to mirror organizational structures. By allowing the frontend team to manage asset injection, we can reduce the friction between teams and streamline development.  


#### Motivation  
Our team consists of separate backend and frontend teams, working with different programming languages. Currently, backend engineers must understand Vite's manifest format and implement a custom code generator to inject the correct assets. Ideally, Vite-related concerns should be maintained by the frontend team, as this better reflects our team's structure and expertise.  


### Suggested solution

 I propose introducing a new option: `build.generateBackendIntegrationHtml`.  

When enabled, Vite will generate a file named `.vite/backend-integration-html.json`, which provides pre-generated HTML snippets for embedding assets into backend templates. This eliminates the need for backend frameworks to parse `manifest.json` and construct `<script>` and `<link>` tags manually.  

Example `.vite/backend-integration-html.json`:
```json
{
  "views/foo.js": {
    "head": {
      "afterBegin": "",
      "beforeEnd": "<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"assets/foo-5UjPuW-k.css\" />\n<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"assets/shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css\" />\n<script type=\"module\" src=\"assets/foo-BRBmoGS9.js\"></script>"
    },
    "body": { "afterBegin": "", "beforeEnd": "" }
  }
}
```

Each entry corresponds to an entry point in the project and contains predefined HTML snippets for different locations within a template (e.g., inside `<head>` or `<body>`).  

The property names (`afterBegin`, `beforeEnd`) are inspired by [`insertAdjacentHTML`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/insertAdjacentHTML), making it intuitive for developers familiar with DOM manipulation.  

This structure allows backend frameworks to simply read and insert the required tags without additional processing.  

### Alternative

_No response_

### Additional context

title: `vite build` produces incorrectly flattened nested CSS
body:
### Describe the bug

When using modern CSS with nesting, a production build will generate invalid CSS.

Given the following CSS:
```css
.foo {
  :where(& > .bar) {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

In a production build, this is flattened as:
```css
.foo :where(>.bar){color:red}
```
This CSS is invalid because `:where(…)` doesn't accept relative selectors.

But I expect it to be flattened as this instead:
```css
:where(.foo>.bar){color:red}
```

---

Note: in dev mode (`vite dev`) it works as expected.


### Reproduction

https://github.com/RobinMalfait/vite-incorrect-css-flattening

### Steps to reproduce

- `npm install`
- `npm run dev` — open http://localhost:5173, the text should be red
- `npm run build` — open http://localhost:4173, the text should be red, but is black

title: css && selector is not working properly during build
body:
### Describe the bug

When I write the following css module:

```css
.hi {
  && {
    color: blue;
  }

  color: red;
}
```

I expect

```css
._hi_ffrjt_1._hi_ffrjt_1{color:#00f}
._hi_ffrjt_1 {color:red;}
```

But I get:

```css
._hi_ffrjt_1{color:red;color:#00f}
```

This is not the specificity I was expecting and is causing bugs for me, specifically when using CSS modules `composes` property. I think the minifier is trying to be smart(?) but it doesn't work with CSS modules

title: Resolve the need for custom arguments
body:
### Description

As a developer, I need to pass custom arguments to build. 

I recently converted a mid-size project from `webpack` to `vite` and this was a major pain point.

This has been discussed a few times already, but non of the suggested solutions seems particularly good.

Since `vite` positions itself as a build system that is very customizable and intended to be built upon, it's pretty much expected that big projects will need to parametrize their build. Therefore I'd object to a comment that this is [out of scope](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/1554#issuecomment-761182562) for Vite.

### What's actually needed?

 - Some way to pass parameters to vite that changes the behaviour of the build (e.g. `--analyze`, `--release`, `--target <platform>`)
 - It's very common to add shortcuts for common sets of parameters to `"scripts"` in package.json (e.g.  `yarn build:android`
    -  These should still allow passing more parameters like `yarn build:android --release` 
 - The mechanism has to be portable between platforms



### Suggested solution

There are a few ways to go about this, some of them have been proposed before:

 - Accept unknown arguments from the CLI and (optionally) pass them through to the build config (or just keep them in `argv`)
    - This [has been rejected](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/7065#issuecomment-1114139804) with the reason that adding a parameter to `vite` itself would be a breaking change, which is a reasonable concern

 - Follow what `npm` or `cargo` does - allow pasting custom parameters after a delimiter (e.g. `--`)
    - `--` specifically doesn't work for `package.json` shortcuts because it's already used by `npm`, `yarn` throws a warning
    - something like `--custom-args` could work, but it should probably be something shorter
        - note that it has to be just a delimiter, not a parameter with an argument, to support appending more arguments when used with `yarn run`

 - Customize the build with environment variables
    - this has been suggested as a solution in previous issues, but it has a few problems
        - passing them through command line is not portable (works differently on windows/linux)
        - using env files instead means you have to create potentially a power set of all possible combination of parameters
           - similar can be set about multiple custom `vite.config.ts files

 - Wrap the CLI in a custom `build.js` 
    - This is what I did in the end:

```javascript
const validArgs = [
  "--release",
  "--no-checker",
  "--android",
  "--ios"
]
// filter out our arguments from `process.argv` fo avoid vite error and put them into custom environement variable
const BUILD_ARGS = [];
const rest = []
for (const arg of process.argv) {
  if (validArgs.includes(arg)) {
    BUILD_ARGS.push(arg);
  } else {
    rest.push(arg)
  }
}

process.env.BUILD_ARGS = BUILD_ARGS.join(' ');
process.argv = rest;

import('./node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js')
```

  - This solves all the issues, but it feels a bit hacky
      - it's not mentioned in the documentation as a supported pattern
      - relies on the `/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js` always being an entry point
      - modifying built in arguments and envirnoment seems problematic
      - custom env variable has to be parsed in vite config file again

A potential solution would be to "bless" the wrapper pattern to make sure it's supported going forward. Notably mention it in the docs with some recommendations and best practices

Probably the nicest form of that would be to export entrypoint function like `startCLI(env, args, customArgs)`,  to avoid the need to mess with the `process.*` variables. Custom arguments could then be passed down to the config.

### Alternative

_No response_

### Additional context

This has been discussed in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/7065 https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/1554 and https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/2891

title: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module only in preview mode, not in dev mode
body:
### Describe the bug

Hello
I've built a Svelte design system (lib) using SvelteKit.
One of my component async import an asset from another folder of the lib :

```js
const data = (await import(`../../lottie/${name}.json`)).default;
```

This component displays an animated icon.
Then i package my lib and publish it
In my consuming app, i `npm install` my lib
Then `npm run dev` everything’s fine, the icon is loaded on the page

If i `npm run build` and `preview` , i get this error :
 
`Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module
https://localhost:4173/_app/lottie/newspaper.json`

It seems that this relative path starts from generated files from SvelteKit and not from node_modules folder where my lib lives.

How can i resolve correctly this path ?

title: Incorrect dead code assumption on production mode
body:
### Describe the bug

During production build, a part of code incorrectly gets removed which is not removed during dev mode

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-new1edjc

### Steps to reproduce

In the repro link, during dev, the value of `config1ValueForSomeComponent` is `config1DefaultValue` and is shown in the HTML.

However, after `npm run build && npm run preview`, the value of `config1ValueForSomeComponent` is `undefined` as can be seen in the built preview HTML.

The code in question is:

```JS
const config = {
  someComponent: { someOtherConfig: false },
  default: { config1: 'config1DefaultValue' },
};

const config1ValueForSomeComponent =
  (config.someComponent || config.default).config1 || 'config1DefaultValue';
```

Here, `config1ValueForSomeComponent` is set to use the `config1` property of either `config.someComponent` or `config.default`. Since the `config.someComponent` is an object, it should use the `config1` property of that object. But since that object does not have `config1` property, the value will be `undefined` and therefore the fallback of `config1DefaultValue` should be used. 

However, in prod. build, the fallback code `|| 'config1DefaultValue'` is stripped off and the value of `config1ValueForSomeComponent` is set to `undefined`.

title: Importing public files with `/* @vite-ignore */` dynamic imports throws an error
body:
### Description

My project generates JavaScript templates for non-technical users.  Before Vite, I published a zip file that looked like this:

- index.html
- config.js
- bundles/
  - mount.js

I'm trying to port this project to Vite.

To prevent Vite from minifying the source and mangling the name, I've tried putting `config.js` in `public`.  However, when I run `vite serve`, I'm met with this error message:

```
Failed to load url /config.js (resolved id: /config.js). This file is in /public and will be copied 
as-is during build without going through the plugin transforms, and therefore should not be 
imported from source code. It can only be referenced via HTML tags.
```

[Reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-ky9uhk?file=public%2Fsecret-number.js,main.js&terminal=dev)

While I respect the effort to prevent people from making mistakes, there ought to be the ability to say "no really, this is on purpose."

**In short, I want to be able to tell Vite _"Treat this JS file like any other asset.  Don't change its name or its contents, and allow it to be imported from the devserver."_**

### Suggested solution

The easiest solution from both an implementation and a user's POV would be a config flag, like `server.allowDangerousPublicDirImports`.  If it's set, Vite skips throwing the error and serves the requested file as if it's any other asset.

This gives the user the final decision about what is and is not permissible in their architecture, without resorting to crazy backdoors like writing a plugin to serve JS as an `assetInclude`.

The term `Dangerous` in the flag name warns people to not set it without consideration.  Using a flag gives it an obvious place to live in the documentation to make it easier for people to find.  (A nod could also be included in `ERR_LOAD_PUBLIC_URL`.) I'm not convinced that the risk of serving files from `publicDir` is so high that they need to individually be whitelisted.

### Alternative

Whitelisting, either by:

1. an inline comment, like `import(/* vite-treat-as-asset */ 'config.js)`, or
2. a config field, like `jsModulesInPublicDir: ['**/*config.js']`.

The comment is less discoverable than a config field, but easier to use.  You explicitly grant permission at the call site, so there is nothing to maintain.  (Imagine if the file name changes.)

A config field is DRYer (for instance, if many packages in a monorepo share a `vite.config`, one setting repairs the whole project).

### Additional context

`config.js` is effectively a JSON with generous commenting and some dependency injection to provide functionality like shuffling and centering.  

It's designed to be hand-edited by people who aren't technical enough to create or maintain a web app, but are capable of editing some strings.  All the complexity is in `mount.js`, which is just a blob to them.  They can edit the config file, drag it to a file server, and have an app that meets their needs without touching the command line.  Moreover, `config` can be generated by a web app after `mount` has already been minted.

title: `mergeConfig` doesn't merge `null` or `undefined` values
body:
### Describe the bug

When using `mergeConfig`, it is impossible to merge `null` or `undefined` values into the base config.

I've encountered this while using Remix ≥ 2.14.0, where `vite.mergeConfig` is used to merge a value for `server.watch` into the base config. This doesn't work for `null` or `undefined` values, which are the only two values Remix tries to merge.
(See [here](https://github.com/remix-run/remix/blob/remix%402.14.0/packages/remix-dev/vite/vite-node.ts#L21) for the `mergeConfig` call and [here](https://github.com/remix-run/remix/blob/remix%402.14.0/packages/remix-dev/vite/plugin.ts#L1053) for the data that's passed into it).
This results in the `server.watch` value never actually being set to anything in the final config, which in turn leads to a whole bunch of files being watched by vite that don't actually need watching during a build.

I'm not sure what the rationale was for [excluding `null` and `undefined` values](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts#L1171) when merging values, but I do see some use-cases for allowing them to be merged, like how remix tries (and fails) to do it.

Without additional context, I would expect any values in the `overrides` record to overwrite the `default` value, no matter what its value is. If I don't want to override a value, I shouldn't include its key in the `overrides` in the first place, so even `undefined` shouldn't receive special treatment as far as I'm concerned.

I've not submitted a PR because I'm not sure what other unforeseen side-effects the removal of that check would have.

I'd also be fine with keeping the check as-is, but then at the very least this quirk should be included in the [documentation](https://vite.dev/guide/api-javascript.html#mergeconfig).

title: Proxy: SSE connection abortion by server is not forwarded to clients
body:
### Describe the bug

This is similar to #13522, but for cases where the server aborts the connection.

When using SSE together with Vite as reverse proxy and the SSE response is aborted from the server side (e.g. server crash), the response channel to the client is not closed and the client has no idea that the server is gone, it just doesn't receive any data anymore.

The following code is my solution for this problem: Listen for `close` events on `proxyRes` (the response received from the proxied server) and if is aborted/errored **and** the client response hasn't been closed yet, destroy the client response.
The second condition is necessary because close events from the client side also trigger abnormal close events on `proxyRes` due to #13578
```ts
proxy.on("proxyRes", (proxyRes, req, res) => {
  proxyRes.on("close", () => {
    if (proxyRes.errored && !res.closed) {
      console.warn(`Proxy response for ${req.url} aborted, destroying client response`)
      res.destroy(proxyRes.errored)
    }
  })
})
```
_Note:_ Using `proxyRes.readableAborted` instead of `proxyRes.errored` should be equivalent, but would require a null/undefined corversion is `res.destroy`. Not sure if that's better or worse.

### Reproduction

not required?

### Steps to reproduce

1. use Vite as reverse proxy for a server providing an SSE (Event Stream) endpoint
2. from any browser, call the proxy SSE endpoint
3. kill the server
4. observe that the client doesn't receive any event

title: Unexpected naming of output chunks when using `cssCodeSplit`
body:
### Describe the bug

I am working on a project  where we have a number of entry points which import a mix of JS and CSS files. Some files are shared, others are not.

Where two different entry points include the same JavaScript and CSS files, the naming of the output chunks is not what I would expect it to be.

As an example:

```ts
// index.ts
import './index.css';

import './some-css.css';
import './some-js.ts';
```

```ts
// index-2.ts
import './index-2.css';

import './some-js.ts';
import './some-css.css';
```

gives the following files:
```
vite v7.1.5 building for production...
✓ 6 modules transformed.
dist/assets/entry-1.css  0.03 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/assets/entry-2.css  0.03 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/assets/some-js.css  0.10 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/my-app-entry-1.js   0.03 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/my-app-entry-2.js   0.03 kB │ gzip: 0.05 kB
dist/shared-chunk.js     0.05 kB │ gzip: 0.07 kB
✓ built in 59ms
```
The unexpected aspect of  this is that it's emitted the contents of `some-css.css` as `some-js.css`

I would expect either:
- `some-js.js` would be emitted with the JS contents and `some-css.css` is emitted with the CSS content, OR
- both files have some shared name related to the file that is importing them, rather than the files being imported.

NOTE: in my real use-case the file names are completely different as the JS and CSS aren't closely related, they just both happen to be imported from the same pair of files. The above is just an example. 

I did some debugging and I think the Vite CSS plugin is allowing Rollup to generate a name for the Chunk, but Rollup can't come up with a good name so it falls back to the name of the last file imported (you can see this in action if you swap the order of the imports in the example). Ideally the plugin would pass a Chunk with just the JS imports to the JS processing and then another chunk with just the CSS imports. It might also be beneficial to give each chunk a name.

Another somewhat related issue is that the CSS asset being output doesn't receive the `originalFileNames` when using a `assetFileNames`/`chunkFileNames` callback which is interfering with my workflow for prefixing the file names with a certain subdirectory from the original file names, but it also prevents working around this issue by using the callbacks to override the name. This appears to be caused by the CSS chunk hardcoding an empty list of original files. If the plugin were to complete all of the metadata for the Chunk it would most likely solve both of these issues.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/jetwiwo/vite-repro-css-js-naming-issue

### Steps to reproduce

Run `npm install` then `npm run build`

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Windows 11 10.0.26100
    CPU: (24) x64 AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor
