title: package.json "exports" with array matcher only takes first
body:
### Describe the bug

I have a monorepo package with a `package.json` file that uses an `"exports"` key like,

```json
{
  "exports": {
    "./*": [
      "./*.tsx",
      "./*.ts",
      "./*.d.ts",
      "./*"
    ]
  }
}
```

It appears that when I import a `.ts` file from this package from an external module, Vite fails to find it, giving me an error,

```
Failed to resolve import '...'. Does the file exist?
```

The filename is `useDebounce.ts`. I know for fact that the file exists, and can even be accessed by control-clicking in VSCode.

See below for the reason this occurs. I debugged the Vite runtime and traced in Vite's source where the actual issue occurs.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-nvvs15ct?file=packages%2Fmy-package%2Fpackage.json

### Steps to reproduce

See the StackBlitz example:

In this example, I put `.ts` first, but imported a `.tsx` file.

The error will occur when running `npm run dev` from the root directory (or from `/apps/main`).

To see that it works when the necessary extension is first in the array, simply swap `.ts` with `.tsx` in the array under `"exports"`.

### System Info

```shell
N/A
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

## Debugger Trace Report

When I debugged Vite's resolution process, I came to this point:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3f1e5a4-0ab3-4bdf-a33b-b51806b41919)

Source position: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/dc5395a27e44066ef7725278c4057d9f1071a53f/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L1020

You can see `useDebounce.ts` is in the list returned from the `resolve.exports` module at index 1, but it appears that `resolveExportsOrImports` blindly takes only the first result, which is `useDebounce.tsx`, which does not exists.

It does appear that there's a spot in [tryCleanFsResolve](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/dc5395a27e44066ef7725278c4057d9f1071a53f/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L628) that attempts to resolve the file with various extensions (including .ts) but it passes the [tryResolveRealFileWithExtensions](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/dc5395a27e44066ef7725278c4057d9f1071a53f/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L1221) function a file with an extension already, in my case useDebounce.tsx. So it tries resolving files like useDebounce.tsx.ts / useDebounce.tsx.json / etc. If this was supposed to catch this case, then this is where the bug actually is.

Otherwise, the issue is that `resolve.exports` responds with a multi-element array, but `resolveExportsOrImports` only regards the first element.

(A temporary work-around is to make sure `./*.tsx` first and use the `.tsx` extension for all files, but this may be impractical for some projects.)

title: Confusing `buildStart` behavior with `createServer` API
body:
### Describe the bug

- Related https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/7479

Vite-node has been using a following style of programmatic server setup https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/94b27af595b5029b6201a7bcf2702169fe7ae6a4/packages/vite-node/src/cli.ts#L86-L99, but I'm not sure whether `buildStart` should be manually triggered on Vite 6 (also how `perEnvironmentStartEndDuringDev` should be enabled on server level or plugin level).

```js
const server = await createServer({});
await server.pluginContainer.buildStart({})
```

One issue with manually calling `buildStart` is that:

```js
// repro1.js
const server = await createServer({
    configFile: false,
    plugins: [
      {
        name: 'repro',
        async buildStart() {
          console.log('[repro:buildStart:in]');
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500));
          console.log('[repro:buildStart:out]');
        },
        transform(_code, id) {
          console.log('[repro:transform]', id);
        },
      },
    ]
});
await server.pluginContainer.buildStart({})
await server.ssrLoadModule("./src/empty.js");
```

which causes `transform` to happen before `buildStart` finishes:

```sh
$ node repro1.js 
[repro:buildStart:in]
[repro:transform] /xxx/src/empty.js
[repro:buildStart:out]
```

Probably this was the cause of https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/7479 and this can potentially break `vite:client-inject` since its `transform` relies on `buildStart`

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/7e7b6608f997fe8e69c891f064edcb7a62740373/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/clientInjections.ts#L102

On the other hand, one issue with not manually calling `buildStart` is that this breaks css import like in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/19606.

```js
// repro2.js
  const server = await createServer({
    configFile: false,
  });
  await server.ssrLoadModule("./src/import-css.js");
```

title: Give us a config to prevent the entire page load and only load the changed file in HMR
body:
### Description

Sometimes when I change a file in VS Code, I see these lines:

Container  | 2025-02-28T17:05:05.955Z vite:hmr [file change] src/Contents/Admin/Menu.jsx
Container  | 5:05:05 PM [vite] (client) page reload src/Contents/Admin/Menu.jsx

I once opened https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/15479, thus I learned one or two things about HMR.

But there is a problem here. My codebase has more than 2000 files. Reloading the page takes 50 seconds. Is it possible to somehow configure Vite and `react-refresh` to just send the currently changed file to the browser?

This is my `Menu.jsx`:

```
import AbcIcon from "@mui/icons-material/Abc"

const ContentsMenu = [
    {
        title: "ContentsContents",
        icon: AbcIcon,
        path: "/contents/parts"
    }
]

export default ContentsMenu
```

It's valid JS. Though it's not a React component, it's valid JS. Each part/module exposes its menu, and then the main `Menu.jsx` which is a valid React component collects those `Menu.jsx` files:

```
import { ContactsMenu } from "Contacts"

const Menu = [
    ...ContactsMenu
]
```

Then the `Menu.jsx` which is a React component imports the main `Menu.jsx` and renders it.

So:

1. Each part/module has a `Menu.jsx` file in which it describes its menu as a simple JS array
2. The main `Menu.jsx` in the application imports and merges `Menu.jsx` from parts/modules and exports them as a simple JS array
3. The `Menu.jsx` component in the admin panel imports the aggregates menu and renders it

This architecture is extremely useful for us. It's valid JS and we have had this architecture for over a decade now (in jQuery, then in Angular.js, then in Angular, then in React).

But whenever we save any of those `Menu.jsx` files that export a JS array, we see a complete page reload which in our huge project causes more than 50 seconds of wait. This extremely degrades the DX.


### Suggested solution

I don't know about the complexities and internals of HMR, but I think letting a simple JS file be loaded without a page reload would be possible. Because it's a simple chain of usage. And we can configure it. For example:

```
{
    hmr: {
        loadIndividually: ["Menu.jsx"]
    }
}
```

### Alternative

No alternative. Right now we're suffering. That's all. We fear changing `Menu.jsx` files. Sometimes we close the browser, change some files together, and then reopen the browser and enter the address to prevent multiple consecutive reloads.

title: Vite 6 does not load `/assets/img/**` as Vite 5 does
body: ### Describe the bug Hello, I'm currently facing two issues while updating to Vite 6. **First one:** I made a plugin to dynamically load images from the `/assets/img` folder we can use `$img('image-path')` to reference any image inside `/assets/img` even if it is in a subfolder like `/img/subfolder/image.png`, this works fine in Vite 5 but does not in Vite 6. Please check attached [Reproduction Repo](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-pqa9sp4z?file=src%2Fplugins%2Fimg.js) and see video below to better understand. i'm using `new URL().href` to obtain image path and then reference it, in my `$img()` plugin we can pass any image path and the function will return the URL to use in `` tags, this is working fine in Vite 5. Just by updating to Vie 6 the function stops working, I read the [upgrade guide](https://vite.dev/guide/migration.html) and research on simimilar issues but any of them solved this problem. **My research** Notice that `img1.svg` is on `/assets/img` and `img2.svg` is on a subfolder of `/assets/img`, I believe the issue comes from the side of Vite 6not being able to deep iterate inside `/assets/img` to see nested folders and images as Vite 5 did, Looks like in Vite 5 all images under `/assets/` were moved to the final app build, but looks like this is no longer the case in Vite 6. I didn't find any configuration to revert that behavior, looks like it is an internal change that generated a breaking change. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69ac5707-bedd-4fc3-89f7-c72c5df927f6 **Second Issue:** This statement works different on Vite 5 than in Vite 6 during Development and Build. One change i found that could be related is this PR #18194 Vite 5: Works fine in both Dev and Prod ```js new URL(`../assets/img/${imgPath}`).href // Returns: `http://localhost/src/assets/img/{imgPath}` // Works fine and returns correct URL to use on Production ``` Vite 6: ```js new URL(`../assets/img/${imgPath}`).href // Returns: `http://localhost/src/assets/undefined` // Does not work with interpolation as used to in Vite 5 // if we switch to "string" + variable it works again but not in production ``` ### Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-pqa9sp4z?file=src%2FApp.vue ### Steps to reproduce 1. `npm i && npm run dev` with vite 5, check images are correct. 2. `npm run build && npm run preview` check images still visible using the function. 3. title: about '\0' prefix, resolvId() retrun the prefixed virtual modules Id, but it isn't prefixed in load() hook.
body:
### Describe the bug

env: vite 6.2.0

About the '\0' prefix. [Link](https://vite.dev/guide/api-plugin.html#virtual-modules-convention. ) 

Office example: 
``` js
export default function myPlugin() {
  const virtualModuleId = 'virtual:my-module'
  const resolvedVirtualModuleId = '\0' + virtualModuleId

  return {
    name: 'my-plugin', // required, will show up in warnings and errors
    resolveId(id) {
      if (id === virtualModuleId) {
        return resolvedVirtualModuleId
      }
    },
    load(id) {
      if (id === resolvedVirtualModuleId) {  // This Line, id isn't has '\0' prefix
        return `export const msg = "from virtual module"`
      }
    },
  }
}
```

But in my plugin, I found that the behavior is inconsistent with the examples on the '\0' prefix.

Office example: The prefixed virtual module id is returned in `resolveId` hook. And then, **the prefixed virtual module id** is used in the `load` hook (  `if (id === resolvedVirtualModuleId) {  ......` ). 
example: id: `'virtual:my-module'`, resolved return: `'\0virtual:my-module'`, in load hook id param: `'\0virtual:my-module'`.

In my plugin development, I found that I return the '\0' prefixed virtual module id in resolveId hook, 
but  it isn't prefixed in load hook. 
example: id: `'virtual:my-module'`, resolved return: `'\0virtual:my-module'`, in load hook id param: `'virtual:my-module'`.

In addition, in configureServer hook, the prefix is the same as in the official website example `/@id/__x00__{id}`

I suspect that the official website example is misleading, or there may be  other reasons.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-1z2fxnqj?file=vite.config.js

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run 'npm install' and 'npm run dev'.
2. Wait for browser loaded, the `Terminal` will print result.

`resolveId` return `'\0'` prefixed id, `load` will print non-prefiexed virtual module id, opposite to office example.

body:
### Describe the bug

I am doing `vite build` + `vite preview --mode test`.

I expect `console.log(import.meta.env.MODE)` to output `test` but the output is actually `production`.

title: Better Support for Debugging Config
body:
### Description

As a developer using Vite I want to be able to debug my code in `vite.config.ts` via VSCode  so I can troubleshoot any problems in plugins or other code snippets added in the file.

I start the debugging by adding `debugger;` statements and then launch vite via: 

* using vite commands in the JavaScript Debug Terminal
* Opening the package.json and hit debug on the inline hint 


### Suggested solution

Vite currently deletes the temporary `node_modules/.vite-temp/vite.config.ts.timestamp-....` file after it was loaded:

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c9e086d35ac35ee1c6d85d48369e8a67a2ba6bfe/packages/vite/src/node/config.ts#L1999-L2012

It would be great if Vite would detect that a debugger is currently attached and keep the file in this case. 

According to [this StackOverflow Post](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67445850) this could be achieved by checking whether there is a inspector url defined (works fine for me in VSCode). But also to check for some [special node argvs](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/9617#issuecomment-326075501) is a potential candidate. 

My proposal would be to use something like: 
```js
import inspector from 'inspector';

function isInDebugMode() {
    const argv = process.execArgv.join();
    return inspector.url() !== undefined || argv.includes('inspect') || argv.includes('debug') || process.env.VITE_KEEP_CONFIG;
}
```

### Alternative

1. Only add an environment variable. (a bit less convienient as you have to remember to set it every time).
2. Add a config key which can be filled by the user to keep the transpiled config.
3. Ensure (somehow?) that sourcemaps are working and breakpoints can be set in the original file directly. Currently source maps are generated but they do not work for VS Code Debugging.  

### Additional context

https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/9617
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c9e086d35ac35ee1c6d85d48369e8a67a2ba6bfe/packages/vite/src/node/config.ts#L1999-L2012

title: Documentation of `build-manifest` is Confusing
body: ### Documentation is - [ ] Missing - [ ] Outdated - [x] Confusing - [ ] Not sure? ### Explain in Detail On the [build-manifest](https://vite.dev/config/build-options.html#build-manifest) part deal with the manifest.json file. When this option is set to true, the build process generates a manifest file at the default location `(.vite/manifest.json)`, which contains a mapping of unhashed asset filenames to their hashed versions for use by server frameworks. However, when the option is set to a string, that string is not only used as the manifest file name but also changes the entire output file path. In this case, the default `.vite` directory and its contents will not be generated; instead, the files are output to a new path defined by the provided string. This behavior may confuse users who expect only the manifest file name to change. ### Your Suggestion for Changes I suggest updating the documentation as follows: ``` When set to true, the build will also generate a .vite/manifest.json file that contains a mapping of non-hashed asset filenames to their hashed versions, which can then be used by a server framework to render the correct asset links. When the value is a string, it will be used as the manifest file name. ::: tip Note: When this option is set to a string, that string will be used as the manifest file name, and the default .vite directory along with its contents will not be generated. Instead, the files will be output to a new path as defined by the string. ::: ``` This clarification will help ensure users fully understand the impact of using a string value for this configuration option. ### Reproduction _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce ## set `manifest` of `true` ## set `manifest` of `manifest.json`

body:
### Describe the bug

`import asset from './example.json?no-inline` is not enough to get a string URL of the asset location. Instead, it imports the asset as an object.

Meanwhile, `import asset from './example.json?url'` imports the asset as a base64 string if it's small enough to be inlined.

Alternatively, combining `url` and `no-inline` provides the URL string but the type definition doesn't exist.
```js
import asset from './example.json?url&no-inline'; // type error

title: Share chunks between multiple ESM Workers
body:
### Describe the bug

When bundling WebWorkers in the `es` format, all the modules imported by the worker are inlined inside the worker chunk and no import syntax is used.

In the following reproduction, there's the following setup:

* 2 script outputs: `main` and `seconday`
* One module `validation` that is imported by `main.ts` and `secondary.ts`

By analyzing the build output, 3 chunks are emitted:
- `validation-[hash].js`, which includes the code shared between both `main` and `secondary` outputs.
- `main-[hash].js`, the code for the `main` output.
- `secondary-[hash].js`, the code for the `secondary` output.

For WebWorkers in ESM format, the same behaviour is expected: instead of inlining the imported modules in the worker's chunk, the worker should import from another common chunk.

Specifically, in the reproduction, I expect the shared chunk to contain the contents of ``isBool`` (from ``validation.ts``) and comlink's ``expose`` and that both are imported by the workers (``FancyWorker1`` just needs to import ``expose``).

To better see the problem, minification is already disabled.

title: Running `vite dev` doesn't exit with an error when there is a problem in the dependency optimisation step (esbuild)
body:
### Describe the bug

Currently in the Ember project we are using the command `vite optimize` to verify that all the dependencies are being optimised correctly (see [this test file](https://github.com/embroider-build/embroider/blob/main/tests/scenarios/vite-dep-optimizer-test.ts) if you're curious). With the recent deprecation of the `vite optimize` command https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/19348 we need a way to be able to verify the dependency optimisation step passes without error in our CI.

We can't rely on `vite dev` for this information because an esbuild plugin fails for any reason that dependency just gets externalised and will be re-loaded once the Vite dev server starts. You can see that behaviour in the linked reproduction.

title: Performance issue: `vite dev` faster after running `vite build` once
body:
### Describe the bug

Hi,

I figured out that my `vite dev` starts faster if I do a `vite build` before.

It does not make any sense to me, so I did some research.

First I thought it was related to `node_modules/.vite` cache, so I played with it being present or not, but it wasn't that.

Then I found `/tmp/node-compile-cache`, and it was responsible of making my `vite dev` faster.

I also tried to run the commands with the `--debug` flag, and what seemed to be significantly faster was the configuration file loading, when `/tmp/node-compile-cache` entries are present.

title: Rollup-Incompatible getModuleInfo behavior
body:
### Describe the bug

This tiny plugin always succeeds in rollup (and `vite build`) and always fails in `vite dev`:

```js
{
  name: 'example",
  load(id) {
    if (!this.getModuleInfo(id)) {
      throw new Error(`load should always see module info`);
    }
  },
}
```

Rollup promises to construct moduleInfo synchronously when any `load` is first started, and even shows an example of calling `this.load({ id })` *and not awaiting the promise* as a way to force `this.getModuleInfo(id).meta` to exist.

I think this disconnect is at the root of issues like https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/6766. 

From some [commentary](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7477#discussion_r860395660) on a related PR it sounds like it's a goal for Vite's module graph to not contain modules that haven't finished loading yet, but if that is true `getModuleInfo` needs to be driven at least partly from a different source of truth that *does* have entries for not-yet-loaded modules.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-vwpnu8sf?file=vite.config.js

title: Vite SSR doesn't overwrite `*` re-export by named export
body:
### Describe the bug

Example code

- dep.js

```js
export const a = "dep-a"
export const b = "dep-b"
export const c = "dep-c"
```

- main.js

```js
export const a = "main-a"
export * from "./dep.js"
export const c = "main-c"
```

#### expected

```sh
❯ node -e 'import("./src/main.js").then(console.log)'
[Module: null prototype] { a: 'main-a', c: 'main-c', b: 'dep-b' }
```

(Also rollup output on [repl](https://rollupjs.org/repl/?version=4.34.8&))

#### actual

```sh
# get "dep-a" instead of "main-a"
❯ node repro.js
{"a":"dep-a","b":"dep-b","c":"main-c"}
```

Side note: Current Vite SSR works if `export const` comes after `export *`. But, probably export hoisting PR https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/18983 currently breaks this pattern all the time. I think technically this is solvable if we gather local named export names first and then pass and exclude them from `exportAll` runtime function:

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c0e3dba3108e479ab839205cfb046db327bdaf43/packages/vite/src/module-runner/runner.ts#L407

title: `?url` query import sometimes returns asset itself instead of url when used in external package with `optimizeDeps.exclude`
body:
### Describe the bug

`?url` query in external package is not recommended anyways, but the behavior seems fishy, so let me record the issue.

Not-so-minimal repro is this sample app with `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-5zkgmuhg?file=vite.config.ts, which includes a following code:

- `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi/parser.wasi-browser.js`

```js
import __wasmUrl from './parser.wasm32-wasi.wasm?url'
```

When starting vite dev initially, wasm file is served properly via

- `parser.wasi-browser.js?v=6c37f146`

```js
import __wasmUrl from "/node_modules/.pnpm/@oxc-parser+binding-wasm32-wasi@0.58.1/node_modules/@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi/parser.wasm32-wasi.wasm?import&url"
```

- `parser.wasm32-wasi.wasm?import&url`

```js
export default "/node_modules/.pnpm/@oxc-parser+binding-wasm32-wasi@0.58.1/node_modules/@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi/parser.wasm32-wasi.wasm"
```

But after restarting the server with `r` and reloading the page, I see a following error in the console:

```
parser.wasm32-wasi.wasm:1 Failed to load module script: Expected a JavaScript module script but the server responded with a MIME type of "application/wasm". Strict MIME type checking is enforced for module scripts per HTML spec.
```

and network tab indicates `parser.wasm32-wasi.wasm?import&url` is now returning wasm binary itself instead of  `export default "...url..."`.

I tried a smaller repro https://stackblitz.com/github/hi-ogawa/reproductions/tree/main/vite-optimize-deps-exclude-url-query?file=test-dep%2Findex.js, but this didn't reproduce.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-5zkgmuhg?file=vite.config.ts

### Steps to reproduce

- Open stackblitz
- `pnpm run dev` starts working app
- Press `r + enter` in terminal and reload page (it might need several tries)
- See `Expected a JavaScript module script but the server responded with a MIME type of "application/wasm"` in the console

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Linux 5.0 undefined

title: Order of glob imported modules should be alphabetical
body:
### Documentation is

- [ ] Missing
- [ ] Outdated
- [x] Confusing
- [ ] Not sure?

### Explain in Detail

In [Features#Glob Import](https://vite.dev/guide/features#glob-import) all examples in generated code show something like:
```js
import * as __glob_0_0__ from "./foo.js"
import * as __glob_0_1__ from "./bar.js"
```
and in every example `foo` is before `bar`, but in reality glob and dir APIs return in almost alphabetical order: `bar` then `foo`.

### Your Suggestion for Changes

Show `bar` before `foo` in generated example results.

_No response_

title: Yarn, VSCode, react-ts, cannot find modules on new project
body:
### Describe the bug

I have run `yarn create vite my-app --template react-ts` and it has generated a project.

The project is not happy at all in VsCode and can not find any of the imported modules.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/748512e2-07c2-4923-b184-8b10ea9a4eb7)

enableGlobalCache: false

title: Vite module runner stacktrace on first line is incorrect
body:
### Describe the bug

Yet another very minor stack trace issue. It's likely due to `"use strict"` appended on runtime side evaluation. Recording it here so I have a place to point to for one test failure on oxc module runner https://github.com/vitejs/rolldown-vite/pull/85.

- repro3.js

```js
throw new Error('__TEST__')
```

- vite2.js

```js
import { createServerModuleRunner } from "vite";
import { createServer } from "vite";

async function main() {
  const server = await createServer({ configFile: false})
  const runner = createServerModuleRunner(server.environments.ssr, {
    // same issues for any interceptor
    sourcemapInterceptor: "prepareStackTrace"
  });
  await runner.import(process.argv[2]);
}

main()
```

On Node:

```js
$ node repro3.js
file:///dir/repro3.js:1
throw new Error('__TEST__')
      ^

Error: __TEST__
    at file:///dir/repro3.js:1:7

### Describe the bug

Looking at the compiled output, it looks like 6.1.x reverted back to the old keyword `assert` for dynamic imports instead of `with` -- is this expected?

#### 6.1.x
```js
const outputFilePath = path.join(PATHS.source, outputFile);
const outputData = await import(outputFilePath, { assert: { type: 'json' } });
```

#### 6.0.1
```js
const outputFilePath = path.join(PATHS.source, outputFile);
const outputData = await import(outputFilePath, { with: { type: 'json' } });
```

```sh
node:internal/modules/esm/assert:88
        throw new ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING(url, 'type', validType);
              ^

TypeError [ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING]: Module "file:///Users/johnny/path/to/my/data.json" needs an import attribute of "type: json"
    at validateAttributes (node:internal/modules/esm/assert:88:15)
    at defaultLoad (node:internal/modules/esm/load:129:3)
    at async ModuleLoader.loadAndTranslate (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:516:32)
    at async ModuleJob._link (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:115:19) {

Node.js v23.6.0
error Command failed

Checked [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/import#importing_modules_with_a_non-literal_specifier) again to make sure variables are OK to use. title: Transitive dependencies of linked dependencies are bundled in SSR build
body:
### Describe the bug

I have a pnpm monorepo containing packages `app` and `shared`. `app` depends on `shared`.

My expectation is that
- Vite will bundle `shared` in `app`'s SSR build for HMR, because it is a linked dependency and therefore is not externalized.
- `shared`'s dependencies in `shared/node_modules` remain external.

What actually happens is that Vite bundles `shared`'s dependencies into `app`'s SSR build as well as `shared` itself. This breaks our app because `shared` pulls in a CJS module (`require-in-the-middle`) which explodes if it is loaded in an ESM context (https://github.com/nodejs/require-in-the-middle/issues/110).

### Reproduction

https://github.com/haines/vite-ssr-externals-repro

### Steps to reproduce

Clone the repo and run `pnpm run repro` (which is equivalent to running `pnpm install` followed by `pnpm run build` and `pnpm run preview` in the `app`).

The SSR bundle `packages/app/dist/server/entry-server.js` will include `require-in-the-middle` rather than importing it from `packages/shared/node_modules`. This will cause the server to blow up with 

```
ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope, you can use import instead
This file is being treated as an ES module because it has a '.js' file extension and 'vite-ssr-externals-repro/packages/app/package.json' contains "type": "module". To treat it as a CommonJS script, rename it to use the '.cjs' file extension.
```

title: Dependencies added during a CSS transform opt-out of HMR
body:
### Describe the bug

When using `addWatchFile(…)` inside a `transform` hook on CSS files, the watched files will successfully trigger a rebuild of the CSS file whenever they change.

However, a rebuild triggered from the watched files will always cause a hard-refresh instead of a HMR refresh of the Stylesheet that happens when the CSS file changes on it's own.

This can be reproduced by a plugin like this:

```ts
function plugin(): Plugin {
  return {
    name: "my-plugin",
    async transform(content: string | undefined, id: string) {
      if (id.endsWith("main.css")) {
        this.addWatchFile(
          fileURLToPath(new URL("./articles/test.txt", import.meta.url))
        );
        return `/* ${Math.random()} */\n${content}`;
      }
    },
  };
}
```

In Tailwind CSS, we use `addWatchFile(…)` extensively to avoid setting up our own watchers. 


### Reproduction

https://github.com/philipp-spiess/vite-css-dependency-hard-refresh

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
pnpm build
pnpm vite dev
touch src/index.css # This triggers a HMR
touch artilces/test.txt # This triggers a hard-refresh
```

This is very minor difference, so it's not likely this matters for any users, but putting here for the record.

- repro2.js

```js
import { repro2Dep } from "./repro2-dep.js"

```

export function repro2Dep() {

title: Svelte CSS treeshaking not working
body:
### Describe the bug

We want to use the svelte kit library (building based on vite) configuration to build a component library that we integrate into a svelte kit app. When we import components as modules. For example like this:
```jsx
import { Heading } from "svelte-kit-library";
```
Then we get in the build files all css stylings of other components that are not used or imported in the application. If the components are imported explicitly, there are no unwanted stylings in the build files.
```jsx
import Heading from "svelte-kit-library/Heading.svelte";
```


### Reproduction

https://github.com/tomolenet/svelte-kit-treeshaking

### Steps to reproduce


In `packages/svelte-kit-app` we use the `packages/svelte-kit-library` in `src/routes/+page.svelte`. First use the module import in line 7.

```jsx
import { Heading } from "svelte-kit-library";
```

```bash
# build app
npm run build -w packages/svelte-kit-app

```

Now check the output `packages/svelte-kit-app/.svelte-kit`. If you search for `.unwanted` which is styling of the `Unwanted` component of `packages/svelte-kit-library` you realize that styling exists in the build result. However, we have not imported the component at any point in the project.  
Now change the import statement and use explicit import in line 10.

```jsx
import Heading from "svelte-kit-library/Heading.svelte";
```

```bash
# build app
npm run build -w packages/svelte-kit-app

```

Now the `.unwanted` class is no longer included in the build. It seems that the tree shaking does not work correctly at this point.

title: Option to prevent `link[rel="stylesheet"]` elements in index.html from being merged into a single `link[rel="stylesheet"]` element
body:
### Description

> As a developer using Vite
> I want multiple `link[rel="stylesheet"]` elements I put in index.html not being merged into a single `link[rel="stylesheet"]` element
> so that I can utilize each individual global stylesheet separately.

It seems that CSS WG is willing to lift the restriction on constructed flag for adoptedStylesheets: <https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/10013#issuecomment-2165396092>.
After the restriction is lifted, we can easily apply the stylesheet of one of the global `link[rel="stylesheet"]` to Shadow Roots.
(Even if the restriction is not lifted, we still have workarounds.)

<details open>
<summary>Example (vanilla + SCSS)</summary>

> https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-orv9nq?file=index.html
> `npm run dev` works as expected because CSS files are not merged during dev.
> `npm run build && npm run preview` doesn't work, because CSS files have been merged into a single file, and the element `link#bgRed` has gone.
</details>

Currently, since Vite always merge `link[rel="stylesheet"]` elements in index.html, we cannot do it this way.

### Suggested solution

Add an option, like:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    cssCodeSplitInIndexHtml: true
  },
});
```

to make `link[rel="stylesheet"]` elements in index.html not being merged.

### Alternative

- loading global styles using JavaScript, so that they can be separated: FOUC.
- putting global styles in index.html as well as loading them using JavaScript: duplication.

### Additional context

I opened a discussion some days ago: <https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/18632>.

title: Generate HTML Snippets for Backend Integration
body:
### Description

#### Background  
Vite provides the `build.manifest` option, which helps integrate with backend frameworks by describing the relationships between built JavaScript and CSS files. Backend frameworks typically parse `manifest.json` and generate `<script>` and `<link>` tags accordingly, embedding them into their templating systems.  

https://vite.dev/guide/backend-integration

Example `manifest.json`:
```json
{
  "views/foo.js": {
    "file": "assets/foo-BRBmoGS9.js",
    "name": "foo",
    "src": "views/foo.js",
    "isEntry": true,
    "imports": ["_shared-B7PI925R.js"],
    "css": ["assets/foo-5UjPuW-k.css"]
  }
}
```

#### Feature Proposal  
Instead of requiring backend frameworks to process `manifest.json` and generate HTML tags, Vite could provide an option to generate the necessary `<script>` and `<link>` tags directly. This would simplify integration with server-side frameworks, reducing the need for custom parsers or code generators on the backend side.  

According to Conway’s Law, system design tends to mirror organizational structures. By allowing the frontend team to manage asset injection, we can reduce the friction between teams and streamline development.  


#### Motivation  
Our team consists of separate backend and frontend teams, working with different programming languages. Currently, backend engineers must understand Vite's manifest format and implement a custom code generator to inject the correct assets. Ideally, Vite-related concerns should be maintained by the frontend team, as this better reflects our team's structure and expertise.  


### Suggested solution

 I propose introducing a new option: `build.generateBackendIntegrationHtml`.  

When enabled, Vite will generate a file named `.vite/backend-integration-html.json`, which provides pre-generated HTML snippets for embedding assets into backend templates. This eliminates the need for backend frameworks to parse `manifest.json` and construct `<script>` and `<link>` tags manually.  

Example `.vite/backend-integration-html.json`:
```json
{
  "views/foo.js": {
    "head": {
      "afterBegin": "",
      "beforeEnd": "<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"assets/foo-5UjPuW-k.css\" />\n<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"assets/shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css\" />\n<script type=\"module\" src=\"assets/foo-BRBmoGS9.js\"></script>"
    },
    "body": { "afterBegin": "", "beforeEnd": "" }
  }
}
```

Each entry corresponds to an entry point in the project and contains predefined HTML snippets for different locations within a template (e.g., inside `<head>` or `<body>`).  

The property names (`afterBegin`, `beforeEnd`) are inspired by [`insertAdjacentHTML`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/insertAdjacentHTML), making it intuitive for developers familiar with DOM manipulation.  

This structure allows backend frameworks to simply read and insert the required tags without additional processing.

title: `vite build` produces incorrectly flattened nested CSS
body:
### Describe the bug

When using modern CSS with nesting, a production build will generate invalid CSS.

Given the following CSS:
```css
.foo {
  :where(& > .bar) {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

In a production build, this is flattened as:
```css
.foo :where(>.bar){color:red}
```
This CSS is invalid because `:where(…)` doesn't accept relative selectors.

But I expect it to be flattened as this instead:
```css
:where(.foo>.bar){color:red}
```

---

Note: in dev mode (`vite dev`) it works as expected.


### Reproduction

https://github.com/RobinMalfait/vite-incorrect-css-flattening

- `npm run dev` — open http://localhost:5173, the text should be red

title: css && selector is not working properly during build
body:
### Describe the bug

When I write the following css module:

```css
.hi {
  && {
    color: blue;
  }

  color: red;
}
```

I expect

```css
._hi_ffrjt_1._hi_ffrjt_1{color:#00f}
._hi_ffrjt_1 {color:red;}
```

But I get:

```css
._hi_ffrjt_1{color:red;color:#00f}
```

title: Resolve the need for custom arguments
body:
### Description

As a developer, I need to pass custom arguments to build. 

I recently converted a mid-size project from `webpack` to `vite` and this was a major pain point.

This has been discussed a few times already, but non of the suggested solutions seems particularly good.

Since `vite` positions itself as a build system that is very customizable and intended to be built upon, it's pretty much expected that big projects will need to parametrize their build. Therefore I'd object to a comment that this is [out of scope](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/1554#issuecomment-761182562) for Vite.

### What's actually needed?

 - Some way to pass parameters to vite that changes the behaviour of the build (e.g. `--analyze`, `--release`, `--target <platform>`)
 - It's very common to add shortcuts for common sets of parameters to `"scripts"` in package.json (e.g.  `yarn build:android`
    -  These should still allow passing more parameters like `yarn build:android --release` 
 - The mechanism has to be portable between platforms



### Suggested solution

There are a few ways to go about this, some of them have been proposed before:

 - Accept unknown arguments from the CLI and (optionally) pass them through to the build config (or just keep them in `argv`)
    - This [has been rejected](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/7065#issuecomment-1114139804) with the reason that adding a parameter to `vite` itself would be a breaking change, which is a reasonable concern

 - Follow what `npm` or `cargo` does - allow pasting custom parameters after a delimiter (e.g. `--`)
    - `--` specifically doesn't work for `package.json` shortcuts because it's already used by `npm`, `yarn` throws a warning
    - something like `--custom-args` could work, but it should probably be something shorter
        - note that it has to be just a delimiter, not a parameter with an argument, to support appending more arguments when used with `yarn run`

 - Customize the build with environment variables
    - this has been suggested as a solution in previous issues, but it has a few problems
        - passing them through command line is not portable (works differently on windows/linux)
        - using env files instead means you have to create potentially a power set of all possible combination of parameters
           - similar can be set about multiple custom `vite.config.ts files

 - Wrap the CLI in a custom `build.js` 
    - This is what I did in the end:

```javascript
const validArgs = [
  "--release",
  "--no-checker",
  "--android",
  "--ios"
]
// filter out our arguments from `process.argv` fo avoid vite error and put them into custom environement variable
const BUILD_ARGS = [];
const rest = []
for (const arg of process.argv) {
  if (validArgs.includes(arg)) {
    BUILD_ARGS.push(arg);
  } else {
    rest.push(arg)
  }
}

process.env.BUILD_ARGS = BUILD_ARGS.join(' ');
process.argv = rest;

import('./node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js')
```

  - This solves all the issues, but it feels a bit hacky
      - it's not mentioned in the documentation as a supported pattern
      - relies on the `/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js` always being an entry point
      - modifying built in arguments and envirnoment seems problematic
      - custom env variable has to be parsed in vite config file again

A potential solution would be to "bless" the wrapper pattern to make sure it's supported going forward. Notably mention it in the docs with some recommendations and best practices

Probably the nicest form of that would be to export entrypoint function like `startCLI(env, args, customArgs)`,  to avoid the need to mess with the `process.*` variables. Custom arguments could then be passed down to the config.

### Alternative

_No response_

### Additional context

This has been discussed in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/7065 https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/1554 and https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/2891

title: Incorrect dead code assumption on production mode
body:
### Describe the bug

During production build, a part of code incorrectly gets removed which is not removed during dev mode

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-new1edjc

### Steps to reproduce

In the repro link, during dev, the value of `config1ValueForSomeComponent` is `config1DefaultValue` and is shown in the HTML.

However, after `npm run build && npm run preview`, the value of `config1ValueForSomeComponent` is `undefined` as can be seen in the built preview HTML.

The code in question is:

```JS
const config = {
  someComponent: { someOtherConfig: false },
  default: { config1: 'config1DefaultValue' },
};

const config1ValueForSomeComponent =
  (config.someComponent || config.default).config1 || 'config1DefaultValue';
```

Here, `config1ValueForSomeComponent` is set to use the `config1` property of either `config.someComponent` or `config.default`. Since the `config.someComponent` is an object, it should use the `config1` property of that object. But since that object does not have `config1` property, the value will be `undefined` and therefore the fallback of `config1DefaultValue` should be used. 

However, in prod. build, the fallback code `|| 'config1DefaultValue'` is stripped off and the value of `config1ValueForSomeComponent` is set to `undefined`.

title: Plugins not picking up changes in watch mode when a CSS file is changed
body:
### Describe the bug

I'm using `vite-plugin-dts` (not isolated to this particular plugin) to generate typescript type definitions along with the bundle in watch mode (`vite build --watch`).

It works fine on the initial and subsequent builds. But when I change a CSS file to trigger a re-build no dts files are generated anymore.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-kya2f6cg?file=vite.config.ts,src%2FApp.tsx,src%2FApp.css&terminal=watch

### Steps to reproduce

`vite build --watch` will run automatically. Notice `App.d.ts` is generated in `dist` folder.

title: feat: support to set browser and browser args in vite.config.ts
Vite processes stuck when using `@rollup/plugin-node-resolve` on Windows VMs
body:
### Describe the bug

I typically develop on macOS, and have been working on an app that looks something like this reproduction: https://github.com/stephenlrandall/vite-resolve-test.

The heart of the issue seems to come from components stored outside the root of the project, but that wish to reference dependencies stored in the project. For example, [this component](https://github.com/stephenlrandall/vite-resolve-test/blob/main/external/Component.svelte) references `mathjs`, which is in the main `app/node_modules`. This component is referenced through the `$external` alias. Normally, Vite wouldn't be able to resolve the import in `Component.svelte`, but with `@rollup/plugin-node-resolve` I can add a plugin to Vite that allows it to correctly resolve the import:

```diff
plugins: [
    sveltekit(),
+   nodeResolve({ modulePaths: [path.resolve('./node_modules')] })
],
```

This all works fine, until I move to Windows. (It actually also seems to work on normal Windows systems, but not on Windows VMs.) At this point I run into hanging processes for both `dev` and `build`. (See attached logs.) I've found similar issues across the internet (the most active was https://community.cloudflare.com/t/vite-stuck-in-build/696830, although that seems like a different case and more reliably reproducible).

### Reproduction

https://github.com/stephenlrandall/vite-resolve-test

### Steps to reproduce

From the `app/` folder, install the dependencies and try running either `npm run dev` or `npm run build`.

### System Info

```shell

title: Allow for defining `server.allowedHosts` through environment variables
body:
### Description

Recently a security improvement was introduced to Vite, where Vite now checks if the domain in the `Host` header is configured in `server.allowedHosts` if it is not `localhost`.

This breaks some CodeSandbox examples, because while Vite is listening on `localhost:5173`, users access the server through `https://:id-5173.csb.app` on CodeSandbox. With newer versions of Vite, this returns a 403. Currently, we recommend people to add `.csb.app` to their `server.allowedHosts`, but it would be nice if we also have a way to make this work with no configuration.

### Suggested solution

I was thinking we could potentially solve this in two ways, and I'm curious what you're thinking of the possible solutions:

1. We could hard-code, similar to `localhost`, that `.csb.app` is allowed in `server.allowedHosts`, or:
2. We could add support for defining hosts in `server.allowedHosts` by passing in environment variables. On the CodeSandbox side, we could introduce a default environment variable in all VMs (like `VITE_ALLOWED_HOST=.csb.app`), which would then also be used by Vite for its checks.

I'm a big fan of Vite, I would love to contribute something like this if this makes sense to you!

title: Generate independent JS bundles with no code sharing between bundles (service workers, multi-page apps, multiple library formats)
body:
### Description

As a developer using Vite, I want to be able to generate independent bundles for a service worker and the main app.  I want the service worker bundle to be completely independent of the main bundle to avoid unnecessary imports. Code splitting is less beneficial when the bundles run in different scopes or pages.

### Example

Let's say I have the following file tree:

- main.js (entry point: depends on main_dep.js and shared_library.js)
- main_dep.js
- service_worker.js (entry point: depends on service_worker_dep.js and shared_library.js)
- service_worker_dep.js
- shared_library.js

In this case, Vite generates three chunks because a single invocation of Rollup ensures code is never duplicated:

- main.hash.js: contains main.js and main_dep.js; imports shared_library.hash.js
- service_worker.hash.js: contains service_worker.js and service_worker_dep.js; imports shared_library.hash.js
- shared_library.hash.js

I want Vite to emit two independent bundles, duplicating shared_library.js in each chunk.

- main.hash.js: contains main.js, main_dep.js, and shared_library.hash.js
- service_worker.hash.js: contains service_worker.js, service_worker_dep.js, shared_library.hash.js

### Related use cases

Independent (no code sharing) modules for library mode
- https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/8098: the author said independent modules, but likely meant separate entry points
- https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/7484: author ended up using separate Vite configs
- https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/7047: comment mentions the ability to target multiple output formats like UMD, CJS, and modules.

Multiple Bundles
- [How to do multiple bundles with vite?](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74390015/how-to-do-multiple-bundles-with-vite): Author notes that Webpack and Rollup support multiple bundles and will prefer those tools to Vite.
- https://github.com/innocenzi/laravel-vite/discussions/116: Resolved as implemented. The link is dead, but probably resolved by calling Vite multiple times.
- https://github.com/ElMassimo/vite_ruby/discussions/138: The author had the same goal as this request. Workaround was to call Vite multiple times.

Build slightly different apps
- #2039 (I've also wanted this)

### Suggested solution

In the vite config object, support an array of Rollup options as requested in #2039.

In build mode, invoke Rollup once per array element.

In serve mode, I don't think Vite uses Rollup.

### Pros

- Keep a single vite.config.ts, a single build and serve command.
- Increases flexibility of Vite to cover several requested use-cases.

### Cons

- May differ from the philosophical goals of Vite. 
- May add significant complexity to build command--I'm not familiar enough with Vite internals to know.

### Alternative

1. Add a separate script tag in index.html. A disadvantage is that it's unclear whether a separate module should be independent of the main entry point.

2. Keep the status quo. A reasonable workaround is to use multiple Vite configs or accept code splitting when using multiple entry points. The main downside is that dealing with two Vite configs is significantly more awkward than a single config. Since a web worker is tightly coupled to the app it supports, it seems heavy-handed to require another Vite config.

### Additional context

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/2039 (Support multiple (array) input/output options in rollupOptions): Closed by Evan You
> You can't because vite build runs a single Rollup build. If you want multiple builds, have multiple vite config files and run vite build -c different.config.js

[Rollup tutorial: never duplicates code](https://rollupjs.org/tutorial/#:~:text=Rollup%20will%20never%20duplicate%20code)
Link to Rollup tutorial that declares that Rollup will never duplicate code.

[StackOverflow: Prevent service-worker.js from being bundled with vite / rollup](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71355290/prevent-service-worker-js-from-being-bundled-with-vite-rollup)
Vite config to place service-worker.js at the top level of the directory. Shared code is split to a separate chunk to be imported by the main index.html entry point and service worker entry point.

[How to add multiple inputs and outputs for Svelte rollup config](https://linguinecode.com/post/how-to-add-multiple-inputs-outputs-for-svelte-rollup-config)
Blog post on how to emit multiple bundles in Rollup using an array of Rollup configurations instead of a single object.  Another [blog post](https://gomakethings.com/how-to-bundle-es-modules-into-multiple-formats-with-rollup.js/) on bundling into multiple formats hints that the bundles are likely independent.

title: Simplify environment variable handling
body:
### Description

Today, variable environment handling in Vite is made of the following moving parts:
- `.env` files were the APP environment variables are defined
- `import.meta.env`
- `process.env`
- The `VITE_` prefix that is used to filter which environment variables show up in `import.meta.env`

The current state of the art, relies on `import.meta.env` and `process.env` (a Node-only API) to correctly (and securely) integrate environment variables in a vite-powered application.

Variables starting with `VITE_` will be included in `import.meta.env` in both client and server (SSR) build, while variable without the prefix will be included also be included in `process.env` only in the server build.

I want to argue that while the docs could be improved, the API is inheritely confusing, we have seen developers at qwik include their secrets in a environment variable prefixed with `VITE_` because they thought `import.meta.env` was the only API available to access variables.

### Suggested solution

1. Simplify the decision making: `process.env` is deprecated and never recommended
2. Rename `VITE_` to `PUBLIC_`, so it states clearly the intention of the prefix, `VITE` while on-brand, it does not contain semantic.
3. Change the behaviour of `import.meta.env` for SSR build:
- During SSR build, `import.meta.env` will include ALL the environment variables, with and without the `PUBLIC_` prefix
- During browser build: `import.meta.env` will include ONLY the environment variables with the `PUBLIC_` prefix (like it does currently)

This way, there is no need for `process.env` in modern source code, and the cognitive load is lower for developers since there is a single recommended API to get the variables `import.meta.env` and a clear intention for variables supposed to be public and therefore included in the browser build.

title: Add a way to universally disable sourcemaps
body:
### Description

Since vite produces modern javascript, sourcemaps in development are often unnecessary as there is no significant transpilation that would make debugging difficult without them.

On the other hand, sourcemaps are notoriously difficult to get correct, and if they're ever wrong then it can ruin the whole debugging experience.

While they can be turned off for individual components of vite (e.g. `esbuild.sourcemap` and `css.devSourcemap`), the dev server will still unconditionally inject sourcemaps from any plugin that produces them (like vite-plugin-vue2).

### Suggested solution

Add a setting `server.sourcemap` that can be set to `false` to prevent the automatic injection of sourcemaps that happens here https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/ba62be40b4f46c98872fb10990b559fee88f4a29/packages/vite/src/node/server/send.ts#L59-L63. 

Or, a bit more ambitiously, add a top level `sourcemap` setting that, if set, would supercede `build.sourcemap`, `esbuild.sourcemap`, `build.rollupOptions.output.sourcemap*` and `css.devSourcemap`. I realize that individual plugins could still inject their own inline sourcemaps into their emitted code, but having a single central setting for this would also encourage plugin authors to respect this setting.

### Alternative

Disabling sourcemaps in the browser dev tools can achieve this end, but this has a few problems:
- Is a per-machine setting, so while one project might not benefit from sourcemaps, another project might still need them, requiring repeated toggling through context switches.
- Is a per-machine setting, so if it is known that the sourcemaps for a particular project are problematic, they cannot be turned off for all developers on that project.

### Additional context

This would likely allow users to overcome (not a fix, but at least _allow_ for a workaround) for the following issues:
- https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-vue/issues/33
- https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/5834
- https://github.com/underfin/vite-plugin-vue2/issues/208

title: Library Mode: Able to conditional set options based on the format that is used.
Unable to exclude certain css `@import` statements from getting inlined
body:
### Describe the bug

I'm building a library which exports some css, but also imports some more from a second library. 

The objective I'm pursuing is not to extract CSS files coming from a component library and keep them as imports, since that library itself will be already used by all consumers. Doing so also gets rid of possible specificity issues as the component library is always imported before the library's own styles.

The CSS is simple enough:

```css
/* src/style/styles.css */
@import "@org/componentLibrary/dist/style.css";

@tailwind base;
@tailwind components;
@tailwind utilities;
```

where an import is stated before tailwindcss' own styles. 
Since Vite provides `@import` inlining ([as stated here](https://vitejs.dev/guide/features#import-inlining-and-rebasing)), this import statement gets extracted and the content is merged in the output .css file.

Currently, it seems as there's no way to exclude certain import statements from getting inlined. This should be doable with `postcss-import` (using [`filter`](https://github.com/postcss/postcss-import?tab=readme-ov-file#filter)), however Vite [already uses this plugin internally](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/css.ts#L1268), and it seems like there's no way to configure it. Additionally, providing the postcss plugin in the `css.postCss.plugins` array seems to ignore the plugin (possibly getting skipped as it's a duplicate plugin?).

Is there a way to achieve this result and if not, can a way to exclude imports be proposed so that there's more flexibility here?

These issues/questions seem related:
- https://discord.com/channels/804011606160703521/1121467219101089892/1121467219101089892 (same issue)
- https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/16669 (unability to configure `postcss-import`)

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-t6nqaz

### Steps to reproduce

- run `npm run build`
- see that the import statement has been extracted and inlined in the output css

title: Allow for easier exposure handling on import.meta.env
body:
### Description

The `import.meta.env` object can be used to expose environment variables to the produced (client) bundle, which allows for flexibility to change behavior across multiple (building) environments. To prevent accidental exposure of sensitive information, there is a required `envPrefix` to ensure only a limited subset of variables is exposed to client-facing code.

However, the current system is somewhat bothersome at occasions where someone would want to use shared variables among different apps/build systems and moreover confusing to some people, resulting in them insecurely trying to expose additional information to the `import.meta.env` object (see e.g. #9880, #17701 and #17710).

Also the current implementation has some unexpected results for some; in #17648 this is being improved on by replacing any unset variables with `undefined`; however the handling of directly referencing `import.meta.env` is still surprising to sme.

Therefore I think some redesign of the environment exposure may be an improvement.

### Suggested solution

I think in addition to #17648 the following ideas might improve the current implementation:
1. Allow users to list/declare all allowed environment variables in the config file, potentially even with metadata like fallback values or marking them as required (see 2.), and only replace those (as alternative to the prefix): this would allow for greater flexibility. By naming it something along the lines of `exposedEnvironment`, it could be more clear to developers what the purpose of this environment is. This would basically be a more developer-friendly implementation of the suggestion in https://vitejs.dev/config/shared-options#envprefix.
2. Emit some warning when building a bundle where some environment variable is missing; e.g. scan for any prefix-matching pattern and notify the user if some environment variable is being referenced but not set ("WARNING: Variable VITE_BAR is being referenced but no value found; including environment into output bundle"). Additionally, the converse may be added: emit some warning for exposed environment variables that are not present in the built code.
3. ~~Opt-out of the replacement of the entire `import.meta.env` object, although I think this would not actually solve any issue, but rather just hide it.~~

### Alternative

Update documentation to more clearly describe the current implementation and potential security implications. Although I think the current documentation is quite clear on this, some confusing is still arising as mentioned above.

title: Accept `async` middlewares
body:
### Description

Most Vite middlewares need to be `async` especially because many of Vite's own APIs that you would be calling like `ssrLoadModule` are `async`. However, `middlewares.use` does not accept `async` methods. This makes for a pretty awkward dance to handle promise rejections and worse means that many users will overlook error handling altogether resulting in server crashes

Also, it would make sense for Vite's `errorMiddleware` to be called in the `.catch` when invoking the promise as the rejection handler, but that's impossible for users to do as it's not exported. However, this could be done internally in Vite.

### Suggested solution

Override `middlewares.use` to accept async implementations or add a `middlewares.useAsync` method

### Alternative

- have every consumer [add a workaround for it](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61086833/async-await-in-express-middleware) instead of adding it directly in Vite. also expose the `errorMiddleware` or have every consumer wrap their implementation in a `try`/`catch` so that it can never throw and implement their own custom error handling
- switch away from `connect` to another server implementation which has native `async` handling like koa

title: Support lightningcss "resolver" option
Dev Server: Cache Modules Unconditionally + HMR Cache Invalidation
body:
### Description

For very large applications (such as the monaco editor), caching with `Cache-Control: no-cache` + Etag is good, but it could be even better.
This is the network profile reloading the monaco editor from the vite dev server:

![chrome_sdBF5lIWxz](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/assets/2931520/525b6f5d-0900-4673-a1a4-68fe121e0ae0)

Every request is a 304 Not Modified, but it still takes 1.4 seconds. This is because the browser still does 860 requests to check if the cache is valid. (However, when the dev tools are closed, it is much faster, though I don't know how to measure that - also, usually, while developing a site, the dev tools are opened)


### Suggested solution

If the vite dev server would
* add a `?t=${devServerStartupTime}` to every module link
* send `Cache-Control: max-age=3600` (or bigger value) for modules it serves
* use HMR to make the website do a `fetch(changedModuleUrl, {cache: "reload"})` for every changed module to force-refresh the cache

then, reloading after a change gets down to less than 400ms (with dev tools open):

![chrome_yKzjqBO9Ge](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/assets/2931520/c7cbfcf4-9b27-4e6c-85ca-40cfeea00862)

If nothing changes, the browser doesn't have to fetch anything from the vite dev server.
If something changes, only the cache of the modified modules are invalidated.
If the server restarts and the HMR websocket connection closes, the `?t=...` parameter makes sure the browser does a full reload.

Btw. nice work on this tool!

title: Support bundling `importScripts`
body:
### Description

WASM packages built with emscripten follow a typical pattern where you have .js and .wasm files, and you wrap them in your worker.

Trying to work with the Vite bundler practices as much as possible, your worker.js wrapper may end up looking something like this:

```js
var Module = {
  async instantiateWasm(info, receive) {
    const init = await import('pkg/the.wasm?init')
    return receive(await init.default(info))
  },
  onRuntimeInitialized() {
    console.log('Successfully loaded wasm exports into global namespace!')
  },
}

importScripts('pkg/the.js')
```

Unfortunately the `importScripts` does not bundle the.js - and if you change it to an `import` it will not be able to access [the Module object](https://emscripten.org/docs/api_reference/module.html)

### Suggested solution

Treat calls to `importScripts` the same as an async `import` and bundle their contents

title: Allow custom generate web workers from custom plugins using custom constructors.
body:
### Description

As an author of a library needing both Web Workers and Audio Worklets I want to provide developers (consumers of my library) using Vite, but also WebPack an easy integration of my library using plugins. 

I am using a custom Web Worker constructor with the common syntax to ensure my plugin can configure the bundlers specifically for my workers: `new Environment.alphaTabWorker(new URL('./alphatab.worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: "module" })`. 

Vite only supports workers if they use the default constructors like `Worker` or `SharedWorker`.

It might be the case that application authors have disabled or reconfigured the default worker settings to their needs and still generation of workers for my library should be possible. 


### Suggested solution

I would like to reuse certain functionality of the built-in `worker` and `workerImportMetaUrl` plugins from within my own plugin shipped along my library to create web workers using my own syntax. 

Hence it would be needed that within my plugin I can trigger the built-in mechanisms to generate workers but using my syntax. And this even if for some reasons the default worker functionality is disabled.  

My plugin shoudn't interfere with the user config more than necessary to activate the worker generation hence it would be good if I can implement the relevant bits in my plugin reusing provided functionalities.


### Alternative

Unfortunately due to Angular having WebWorkers disabled by default in the angular.json I opted in my library for a custom syntax and handling of Workers hence changing the syntax to the default `Worker` is maybe not really possible without conflict. 

As a starting point maybe Vite could also just expose a way of configuring the allowed constructors to extend `Worker` and `SharedWorker` with custom strings. But currently the RegExp in both related plugins check for only those strings. 



### Additional context

As a next step I will also have to consider audioWorklets where I will need to generate worker-like entry points. I'm not yet sure if and how Vite supports them but typically the web worker parts can be reused. The tricky part is the handling of transitive dependencies. 

The matched syntax would be `someVar.audioWorklet.addModule(new URL('./myworklet.js', import.meta.url))` or `someVar.addModule(new URL('./myworklet.js', import.meta.url))`.

title: Dev server: Initial call to backend to get cookies
Support server entry — `$ vite path/to/server.js` / `vite.config.js#server`.
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Vite does not support server entries.

For example, the [`playground/ssr-vue/server.js`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/playground/ssr-vue/server.js) file is not processed by Vite which means:
- The user cannot use Vite constants such as `import.meta.env`.
- The user cannot use TypeScript (without using an extra tool such as `ts-node`).
- If the user makes a change to `server.js` then the user has to manually stop and re-start the server.


### Suggested solution

We add an argument to the CLI command `vite`.

```shell
$ vite ./server.js
```

The argument is optional and if omitted Vite behaves as it does today (it starts Vite's built-in dev server).

```js
// server.js

import express from 'express'
import vite from 'vite'

startServer()

async function startServer() {
  const app = express()

  const { middlewares: viteMiddleware } = await vite.createServer({
    server: { middlewareMode: 'ssr' },
  })
  app.use(viteMiddleware)

  app.listen(process.env.PORT || 3000)
  console.log(`Server running at http://localhost:${port}`)
}
```

The whole `vite.loadSSRModule` dance would be taken care of.

We can even consider adding support for HMR and, if HMR is not applicable, to automatically reload the server by killing  `process.env.PORT` with e.g. [kill-port](https://www.npmjs.com/package/kill-port). (It's a common convention to use `process.env.PORT` as server port.)

The user can also define the server entry with `vite.config.js#server`.

```js
// vite.config.js
export default {
  server: 'server.js'
}
```

```shell
# No need to specify the server entry here
$ vite
```

### Alternative

_No response_

### Additional context

This ticket is part of [Vite Server RFC](https://github.com/vikejs/research/issues/3).

title: Feature Request: Exclude some libraries' optimization in node_modules.
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

I need ability to exclude the optimization (bundling & caching) of some files in node_modules. The _"exclude"_ means the module resolution should not append `?v=xxx` to the resolved file and it should always give me latest contents without restarting the vite server.

One possible solution is creating symlinks. However when I created node_modules/x → node_modules/.skip_optimize/x, nothing has changed. After digging into the source code, I think vite made an assumption that all symlinks are out of node_modules:
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/bcb6d753234f1085061e8a6e3623a597bb961ac5/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/resolve.ts#L417

However, keeping files in node_modules has a benefit that it does not hurt node's resolution (see nodejs/node#3402 for more details). Even though vite implements custom resolver, I think it would be good to take this problem into consideration.

_Read more context in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/4429_

### Suggested solution

In the code above, add a check of `optimizeDeps.exclude`. If the requested module should be excluded, then don't return something like `?v=xxx`.

I'm building a library and I want to generate output similar to what popular libraries like React and Vue do: esm + cjs/umd builds for both dev and prod modes, with only prod builds being minified and having source maps.

Right now, library mode generates esm and umd for prod mode by default and I can enable sourcemaps with a single line in the vite config file.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Would be nice to have a builtin option (possibly enabled by default) to also generate dev builds which are not minified and include conditional code that uses `import.meta.env.DEV` (as mentioned [here](https://vitejs.dev/guide/env-and-mode.html)).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

It should be possible to achieve this using `rollupOptions` with custom input/output but I think this is a necessary feature for library authors.

title: Update HMR defaults for `isolated-app:` protocol
body:
### Description

When using Vite as a dev server for an Isolated Web App (see https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/15686#issuecomment-1904609649 for instructions on setting up an IWA and the [README](https://github.com/WICG/isolated-web-apps/blob/main/README.md) for an overview of IWAs) using Chrome's built-in Dev Mode Proxy, the HMR server defaults to the IWA's `hostname`, which is randomly generated and not directly connected to the dev server. Fortunately, what it should connect to is very straight forward and should not change: the server's actual host and port. Updating the codebase to make this the default, while allowing overrides as normal, would make the DX here even more smooth.

### Suggested solution

In the current HMR client script, where it checks if the protocol is `http:` or `https:`, and one more option, `isolated-app:` and, if it's that, set the host and port of the HMR websocket to the server's host and port instead of the window location's host and port. This may need to be injected by the server itself. `localhost` is fine for the host here, if needed.

### Alternative

Documentation could be added for this specific usecase, but because its default configuration would be usable for >80% usecase and the code delta should be fairly small, I think it's a good candidate to be folded into the project itself.

I've also considered creating an IWA plugin for Vite that could handle this as well, but (for now, anyway) it'd amount to about 6 lines of injected configuration, that doesn't feel worthwhile enough as compared to actual core support.

title: Bundling a worker in library mode results in 404 when using the library
body:
### Describe the bug

I'm working on an npm package that makes use of a web worker. The worker makes heavy use of imports, dynamic imports and wasms. Using the library results in a 404 when the worker gets instantiated because it can't be fetched at the absolute path `/assets/worker-{hash}.js`. So far the only option to make everything work is to inline the worker as so:
`import MyWorker from './worker/worker_entrypoint?worker&inline'`

But this unfortunately generates a huge bundle file (tens of MBs given that also the wasms are inlined) and essentially disables code splitting.
I've tried importing the worker differently such as:

- Importing as `?worker`: in the final bundle the worker ends up in `/assets/worker-{hash}.js` resulting in 404 when a user uses the library
- Importing as `?worker&url`: Same as before, using `new URL(worker_as_url, import.meta.url)` makes no difference
- Importing as `?url`: worker file gets simply encoded as base64 with wrong mime type and dependencies are not resolved
- Instantiate the worker with `new Worker(new URL('./worker_entrypoint', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })`: Similar problem as the first point but this time it ends up in `/public/assets/worker-hash.js`

title: Provide an option to include all subdependencies of a nested package in the bundle with optimizeDeps.include
body:
### Description

Currently, when required to exclude some library (`my-lib`) from the bundle (such as for deduping a shared peer dependency) but where `my-lib` has dependencies that may use CommonJS, we are required to do the following:

```
optimizeDeps: {
    exclude: ['my-lib'],
    include: ['my-lib > cjs-dep']
}
```

Which works fine unless you have an ESM dependency which itself uses CommonJS dependencies. This is particularly problematic for arbitrarily nested CommonJS dependencies in third party libraries.

```
optimizeDeps: {
    exclude: ['my-lib'],
     include: ['my-lib > esm-dep', 'my-lib > es-dep > ...', 'my-lib > esm-dep > ... > cjs-dep']
}
```

Identification of the CJS dependencies or even just the dependencies that ought to be added back to bundle is non-trivial and should be avoidable for developers.

Specifically, there is a semantic difference in meaning between these two very close, similar fields - excluding a node severs the tree at that point where as inclusion requires you manually specify each and every individual node in the subtree you've excluded to reconstruct it.


### Suggested solution

For the sake of backwards compatibility, we could keep the default behaviour - though I think it is somewhat counterintuitive (when semantically exclusion cuts the tree off at the node you exclude from)

And make changes to
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/dd610b5f77fb596b3d64f2f7fb94ccce392777a7/packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/index.ts#L841

which allows for some non-glob matching suffix to the package name to indicate that you wish to add sub dependencies of this package to be manually included also > this will probably not work given the failure of the test plugin that added everything automatically, there's probably something better to be done in the dep resolver code that somebody could point me to.

### Alternative

- Writing plugin for dynamically identifying dependencies and adding the entries manually which just grows too large
- Avoiding the need for bundle exclusion, and just including everything instead which destroys DX by removing HMR and requiring --force all the time

I tried writing a plugin to scan for deps of the excluded libraries but this quickly grew to an array of 180k optimizeDeps.include entries and had so many edge cases that it wasn't worth continuing.

### Additional context

Usecase
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/14672

Recent Issue
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/14545

Originally raised as an issue, closed due to inactivity but no resolution
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/9220
